t: The Sheikh Lectures Within the Programme Accompanying the Grand al-Fatih Qur'an Memorisation Competition
a: الشيخ يحاضر ضمن البرنامج المصاحب لمسابقة الفاتح الكبرى لتحفيظ القرآن
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew took part in the programme accompanying the grand al-fatih competition for the memorisation and correct recitation of the qur'an, held between 24/09 and 30/09/2010 in tripoli in the libyan jamahiriyah.

more than 140 competitors from 73 countries, from the various continents of the world, are taking part in the activities of this session, alongside a number of scholars, sheikhs and specialist judges from inside the jamahiriyah and outside it.

the sheikh took part in the programme accompanying the competition with a lecture on reflective engagement with the qur'an (tadabbur): its meaning and its means. he also delivered a number of lectures and scholarly lessons in benghazi.

it may be noted that this competition is organised annually by the general authority for endowments and zakat affairs, and covers two areas: the memorisation of the entire noble qur'an, and the correct recitation of the noble qur'an (tajwīd).

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Holds Several Courses in the State of Sudan
a: الشيخ الددو ينظم عدة دورات في دولة السودان
b:
sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew took part in a symposium held by the higher council for the call to islam (al-majlis al-aʿlā li-l-daʿwah al-islāmiyyah) on the present state of the call to islam (daʿwah), its future, and the challenges facing it. this symposium was attended by a company of scholars, thinkers and callers to islam from the various regions of the world.

the sheikh took part in this symposium with a paper on the intellectual reassessments undertaken by the islamic groups.

during his visit to sudan in the period between 14 and 20/10/2010, the sheikh also carried out several activities in the call to islam, among them:

a scholarly course on concepts and technical terms, which he delivered at the al-nur complex in khartoum.

a scholarly course on three subjects: understanding of the religion (al-fiqh fī al-dīn), sharia-based governance (al-siyāsah al-sharʿiyyah) and islamic transactions (al-muʿāmalāt).

he also delivered a lecture to the higher council of the judiciary in sudan on the proprieties of the judiciary and of the judge.

t: The Sheikh Takes Part in the Board of Trustees Meeting of the International Union of Muslim Scholars
a: الشيخ يشارك في اجتماع مجلس أمناء الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين
b: work began today, friday, on the meeting of the board of trustees of the international union of muslim scholars, held in the qatari capital doha under the chairmanship of his eminence dr yusuf al-qaradawi, president of the union. sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew is taking part in the meeting, whose agenda includes a number of items, among them deliberation on the report of its secretary-general, professor dr ali muhyi al-din al-qaradaghi, and the completion of the election of the members of the union’s executive bureau. his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew has been elected as the officer responsible for the training of scholars in the executive bureau, in addition to membership of the union’s board of trustees. it is worth noting that the international union of muslim scholars comprises more than a thousand scholars in their personal capacity, alongside 70 associations comprising 50,000 muslim scholars.

t: Rejecting Singly Transmitted Reports in the Case of the Qur’an
a: رد خبر الآحاد في القرآن
b:
question: is it also true, as is said, that the companions (may god be pleased with them) entrenched this principle of rejecting the singly transmitted report (ḫabar al-āḥād) when they rejected established reports transmitted singly from individual companions and so did not establish a qur’anic reading on their basis — such as the reading "ten known sucklings" and the reading "so cut off their right hands"?

answer: no, this too is not an instance of rejecting the singly transmitted report. the companions established that the qur’an must be mass-transmitted (mutawātir), so it cannot be narrated by a singly transmitted report; it is different from singly transmitted reports. singly transmitted reports do not occur in the qur’an; they occur in the sunnah only. for this reason the companions did not accept as qur’an anything narrated by a few individuals, except for a single verse which they found written down and for which they found no one who had memorised it except khuzaymah ibn thabit — but the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) had made his testimony count as the testimony of two men. it is the words of god, be he exalted: {there has come to you a messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is your suffering; anxious is he over you; to the believers kind and merciful} (sūrat al-tawbah 9:128). they did not doubt that this was the speech of god and that it had been revealed to the messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) — indeed many of them had heard it. they doubted only whether it had been abrogated in the final review (al-ʿarḍah al-akhīrah) or not. khuzaymah informed them that he had heard it from the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) in his last recitation of sūrat al-tawbah, so they established it therein, because they knew that his testimony counted as the testimony of two men. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: The Authoritativeness of the Singly Transmitted Report
a: حجية خبر الآحاد
b:
question: does this apply to us, the community of muslims, since we act upon singly transmitted hadiths (āḥād) which yield only probability — the import of the noble verse {we do but conjecture, and we are by no means certain} (sūrat al-jāthiyah 45:32)?

answer: no. singly transmitted reports, if they reach us by a sound route, must be acted upon — it is obligatory (wājib) — by agreement. the jurists are in consensus (ijmāʿ) on acting upon the singly transmitted report. that is why al-iraqi said: *and the jurists, all of them, employ it.* "employ it", that is, employ the singly transmitted report, meaning they act upon it in matters of legal ruling. the same holds for the good (ḥasan) report: the good hadith is acted upon by all the jurists. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: Comment on the Maxim "The Unlawful Does Not Attach to Two Liabilities"
a: تعليق على المقولة: الحرام لا يتعلق بذمتين
b:
question: what is the position of the sharia on people’s saying, "the unlawful does not attach to two liabilities (dhimmahs)"?

answer: this is one of the legal maxims (al-qawāʿid al-fiqhiyyah) of the hanafis. people apply it where it does not belong and do not understand it, and it is contrary to the maliki school, which is the school followed in this country. the maliki position is that the unlawful does pass beyond two liabilities; the hanafi position is that the unlawful does not pass beyond two liabilities — meaning that usurpation (ghaṣb) extinguishes ownership, and that theft extinguishes ownership. so if a person usurps something and sells it to another, what the buyer has bought is lawful for him, because usurpation, in the hanafi view, extinguishes ownership. this is unlike the malikis, the shafi’is and the hanbalis: in their view usurpation does not extinguish ownership, so the object remains owned by its original owner, and therefore in their view the unlawful does pass beyond two liabilities. people apply the maxim where it does not belong and understand it in other than its correct sense.

t: The Muslim’s Stance Towards the Scholarly Heritage of the Ummah
a: موقف المسلم تجاه تراث الأمة
b:
question: what is the muslim’s stance towards the heritage of the ummah in jurisprudence and in learning, and what do you advise concerning those who call for abandoning it and relying only on the qur’an and the sunnah, as they put it?

answer: god, glorified and exalted, honoured this ummah with the sending of muhammad (may god bless him and grant him peace) and the revelation of the clear book. the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace) left among it the book and the sunnah, and these two are the root of all knowledge. but the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) also made clear that men’s understandings of the book and the sunnah vary; god made that clear and referred the matter to those who are people of derivation (istiṅbāṭ), and they are "those in authority" in the sharia sense. god, be he exalted, said: {and when there comes to them a matter concerning security or fear, they broadcast it; whereas had they referred it to the messenger and to those in authority among them, those among them who derive [the matter] would have known it} (sūrat al-nisāʾ 4:83). he did not say "they would all have known it". had everyone who merely goes back to the book and the sunnah known the ruling, he would have said: "had they referred it to the messenger and to those in authority among them, they would have known it". but god did not say that; rather he said: {those among them who derive it would have known it}. and these are always few in number; the people of derivation are always few. those among the companions who attained the level of independent legal reasoning (ijtihād) and derivation did not, by ibn hazm’s count, exceed eighteen, and by al-nasa’i’s count did not exceed twenty-two, or only twenty-one. among the successors there was a small number, and likewise among the successors of the successors.

therefore it is impossible for this ummah, with its different races, its various languages and its disparate levels, all to be among "those who derive it" — this can never come about. hence one must return to what god has granted to the people of knowledge, those firmly grounded in knowledge, to whose knowledge god has referred [us] and to which the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace) referred [us], making clear that they are the heirs of the prophets.

whoever wishes to confine himself to the book and the sunnah alone must end by abandoning part of them both. for if he confines himself to the qur’an alone, from where will he obtain the chain of transmission (isnād) and certainty? he will certainly not reach mass transmission (tawātur) in every particular of the qur’an, and so he will then be compelled to follow a qualified scholar (taqlīd) in the particulars, and especially in the modes of recitational delivery, as we have mentioned. that is why al-suyuti (may god have mercy on him) said in al-kawkab al-sāṭiʿ: *……… and the seven [readings] belong definitively to mass transmission; and it is said, except the manner of delivery; it is said, and divergence of wording belongs to the reciters.*

likewise with the sunnah: a person will be forced to encounter hadiths that appear to conflict, and he will be left standing, not knowing the resolution. he will be compelled to investigate the abrogating (nāsikh) and the abrogated (mansūkh), and this requires knowledge of chronology — which of the two came first. he will likewise be compelled into matters of preponderance regarding transmission, the probity of narrators and the like — matters in which a person is a follower (muqallid), dependent upon the history of the ummah and upon its heritage.

for the book and the sunnah were conveyed to us by none but this honoured ummah, by its scholars and its imams. were it not for the scholars of this ummah, neither the book nor the sunnah would have reached us. we did not meet the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace); we did not hear from gabriel; we did not hear from the lord of might and majesty, exalted be his majesty. we heard from the generation whom we met, and they are god’s trustees over the revelation they conveyed to us, and they were entrusted by the generation above them, and those were entrusted by the generation above them, until the chain of transmission ends at muhammad (may god bless him and grant him peace). accordingly a person must respect all his teachers, and must know that the knowledge he possesses is narrated from them and has come by way of them. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: What Can Stand Against a Singly Transmitted Report
a: ما يعارض خبر الآحاد
b:
question: is it true, as is said, that the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) is the one who established the rejection of the singly transmitted report (ḫabar al-āḥād), when he did not act upon what dhu al-yadayn observed until the others testified to the truth of his observation?

answer: this does not entail not acting upon the singly transmitted report. it entails rather that dhu al-yadayn’s report was contradicted by the certainty of the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him): it was a singly transmitted report opposed by something stronger than it — and stronger than a singly transmitted report is the report of the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him). for when dhu al-yadayn asked the messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), saying, "has the prayer been shortened, or did you forget?", he said, "neither of these happened." this is the report of the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him), and it is more truthful than dhu al-yadayn. but afterwards he wavered and doubted; and when he doubted, that required him to ask — because dhu al-yadayn’s report was not strong enough to stand against the report of the messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and what he held with certainty, yet it made him doubt. when doubt arose in him, he sought further knowledge, in accordance with the sharia principle {say: produce your proof, if you are truthful} (sūrat al-baqarah 2:111); and so knowledge came to him through the report of the companions. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: The Condition for Acting upon a Singly Transmitted Report
a: شرط العمل بخبر الآحاد
b:
question: is it a condition for acting upon a singly transmitted hadith (āḥād) that it not contradict the practice of the people of medina (ʿamal ahl al-madīnah) or of others, or that the jurists — or some of them — accept acting upon it?

answer: what we were speaking about concerns the attainment of certainty through a singly transmitted report at the level of rational conviction, not at the level of action. as for action: if the singly transmitted report is sound (ṣaḥīḥ), acting upon it is obligatory (wājib), without searching for a contrary indicant; and if something stronger is found to contradict it, that suspends acting upon it.

in malik’s view, the practice of the people of medina — in what they narrated, not in what they held as considered opinion — is stronger than a singly transmitted report, for he says: "a thousand from a thousand — i do not turn away from their statement." he thus treated it as equivalent to mass transmission in meaning (al-tawātur al-maʿnawī) and on that basis gave it precedence over singly transmitted reports. likewise, in abu hanifa’s view, the practice of the people of kufa; and in the view of some, the agreement of the four imams — abu bakr, umar, uthman and ali.

t: A Question on Following a School of Law in Principle, and on Its Ruling
a: سؤال عن التمذهب أصلا و عن حكمه
b:
question: a question about following a school of law (tamadhhub) in principle and about its ruling, and about the fact that many people call for abandoning adherence to the schools, saying that the scholars who founded the schools took from the book and the sunnah — so why should not all people go back to those two?

answer: this idea is unattainable and burdensome in the age of the later generations, because the book and the sunnah do not cover every question explicitly — do not cover explicitly every newly arising event and novel case. rather, the area of the legally responsible person’s conduct that is covered by revelation is very small; it does not reach 10% of the conduct of the legally responsible. the remainder of the acts of the legally responsible is covered by independent legal reasoning (ijtihād) and derivation (istiṅbāṭ). there is no doubt that ijtihād and derivation are not confined to the people of one time, nor to the people of one place. but the rules by which one deals with the texts are limited by reason. so it is not possible for a person to come today — even if he attained the rank of the predecessors in knowledge — and say, "i shall bring a new position on the import of the general term (ʿāmm), or on the import of the unqualified (muṭlaq), or on the determination of preponderance." he cannot bring anything, because the predecessors have already exhausted all the rational possibilities. what is possible is only combination (talfīq), and this is what has been left to the later generations. there is no harm in talfīq — that a person take from this school such-and-such a rule and from that school such-and-such a rule; but in most cases he will not, in rational matters, go beyond what they have exhausted. matters rationally exhausted cannot admit of renewal.

the schools are not outside the book and the sunnah; rather they cover only the area that revelation does not cover, because what revelation covers, as we have said, does not enter into the definition of jurisprudence (fiqh) at all. fiqh is precisely those matters in which there is no explicit text (naṣṣ) and which are the reasoned judgements of men; and in these there must of necessity arise schools. but of those schools, not one is compulsory upon any person.

rather, if a person is a student of knowledge, he must choose the preponderant (rājiḥ) of the two, because acting upon the preponderant is obligatory (wājib) — not "the preponderant" [in some absolute sense]: he searches out what is preponderant in his own view, and he knows that its being preponderant in his view does not entail its being preponderant in the view of all people. the mere fact that a position is preponderant in your view means that the supporters of that position have increased by one voice; and on the other side you may find that the other positions have many other voices too.

likewise, if he is not fit for this level and is not a student of knowledge at all, then these schools are a latitude that delivers him — as al-sha’rani said. he said: the sharia has two walls, one of them the wall of the standing ruling (ʿazīmah) and the second the wall of the dispensation (rukhṣah), and all the schools lie between these two walls. so if you find a school that is strict on a question, know that it has drawn nearer to the wall of the standing ruling; and if you find a school that is lenient in it, know that it has drawn nearer to the wall of the dispensation. and look to yourself: are you among those who take dispensations, or among the people of the standing rulings? if you are excused by some excuse, or are a person of weakness, then go with those who went to the dispensation; and if you are a person of strength and of ease, then go to those who went to the standing ruling.

t: When Legal Opinions Conflict for the One Seeking a Ruling
a: إذا تعارضت الفتاوى على المستفتي ؟
b:
question: if legal opinions conflict for the person seeking a ruling (mustaftī), which of the two opinions should he act upon — the stricter or the lighter?

answer: this question is a point of disagreement among the legal theorists. some of them said it is not permissible for him at all: if he has been given a considered legal opinion (fatwā) by a reliable authority and is convinced of the jurist’s truthfulness and that this is what his reasoning led him to, it is not permissible for him to seek an opinion from another, lest he fall into conflict. if he does so, or if he was not convinced by the first one’s opinion and is then given a contrary opinion, then at that point he is like one for whom two texts conflict: he strives first to reconcile them, then to determine preponderance. preponderance is either by the evidence, or by the opinion of another person — he asks a third who determines for him which of the two preponderates. if he does not find this and it is not possible for him, then it is said: he takes the stricter, because that is the precaution for his religion; and it is said: he takes the easier, because of the words of god, be he exalted: {he has not laid upon you in religion any hardship} (sūrat al-ḥajj 22:78), and because this religion is the one the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) described in his words, "the most beloved religion to god is the upright and accommodating one (al-ḥanīfiyyah al-samḥah)."

as to a state’s adopting a particular school: this does not mean that people’s conduct will conform to that school. what is meant is rather that the judiciary will proceed in accordance with it, and that public juridical guidance on general matters will be in accordance with it. as for individuals, they act in accordance with what is preponderant in their own view, and it is not permissible for them to abandon the preponderant because the state has adopted one of the schools. this did not occur in any past age. in the days of the abbasids, when they adopted abu hanifa’s school in the judiciary, it did not mean that people abandoned their schools and went over to the school of abu yusuf. likewise in the ottoman state, for example, which adopted the hanafi school: it did not mean that it imposed the hanafi school upon people in their conduct and their acts, but only in what the judge adjudicates — that alone is what is meant. if that judge departed from it on the basis of his own reasoning and acted on what was preponderant in his view and ruled accordingly: if, in the original terms of his appointment, he had committed himself to ruling only in accordance with such-and-such a school, then he is considered removed from that — unless the two litigants accept him, in which case he is like an arbitrator. even so, if he rules by it, his ruling is enforceable, because it removes the dispute.

as to the call to dispense with the schools, or the call to repudiate the schools: this is a novelty, and it did not exist in earlier ages. none of those who lived in the time of the successors of the successors, when the schools arose, denied the existence of the schools; not one of the scholars of the muslims denied that. nor can it be denied at all, because god has made among the ummah peoples who are unable to understand the evidence directly, who are unable to reconcile conflicting evidences, and who do not distinguish the abrogating (nāsikh) from the abrogated (mansūkh). these must return to the people of remembrance, as god, be he exalted, said: {so ask the people of remembrance, if you do not know} (sūrat al-naḥl 16:43). their recourse to the people of remembrance is to ask about their school — because "school" (madhhab) means a way of dealing with the texts followed by the qualified scholar who is competent for that.

as to what we hear today of the revolt against the schools — when one of the students of knowledge, or of the half-educated, is asked about his school and says, "my school is the book and the sunnah, and i do not recognise the schools" — this is on a par with the views of the kharijites of the earliest period, although the kharijites did not repudiate the following of a school. these have gone beyond them in departure: they have departed further than the departure of the kharijites. and therefore the alternative to this, if he is asked, he cannot find — because he himself is unable to derive the rulings of ablution (wuḍūʾ), nor the rulings of the full ritual washing after major impurity, nor others, from the texts directly; and he does not know the difference between the general (ʿāmm) and the specific (khāṣṣ), or the unqualified (muṭlaq) and the qualified (muqayyad); and were he asked about that, he would not be able to distinguish it. even so, many of those who make this claim do not restrain their tongues: whatever subsidiary question they are asked about, they must give an opinion on it with a view that may be the furthest thing from the truth and contrary to the texts, and may be among the worst of understandings of the texts. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: The Difference Between the Explicit Text and the Apparent Meaning
a: الفرق بين النص والظاهر
b:
question: what is the difference between the explicit text (naṣṣ) in the words of god, be he exalted, {and god has permitted trade and forbidden usurious gain} (sūrat al-baqarah 2:275), and the apparent meaning (ẓāhir) in his words {and marry such of the women as seem good to you, two, three or four} (sūrat al-nisāʾ 4:3)?

answer: the explicit text is the expression that indicates its original, immediately understood meaning, that meaning being what the speech intends; and it admits of interpretation (taʾwīl) and of abrogation. the apparent meaning is the expression that indicates a meaning which is not the immediately understood one, that meaning being what the speech intends, and evidence has indicated that it is what is intended. so the explicit text’s meaning is understood from itself, whereas the apparent meaning requires something else to clarify it.

the explicit text in the first verse — "and god has permitted trade" — is a statement from god, glorified and exalted, that he has legislated sale for his servants and made it lawful for them. it is general in scope (ʿāmm), taking in every kind of sale except what has been excepted and forbidden; and the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade fifty-eight kinds of sale, which are excepted from this verse. likewise he forbade usurious gain (ribā): this is an explicit text forbidding ribā absolutely. and the messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) made clear that ribā has seventy-three gateways, and that among them is one like a man having intercourse with his mother — we ask god for safety and well-being. so ribā is of many kinds, and all of them are forbidden (ḥarām) by the explicit wording of this verse, which is clear in that respect.

as for the apparent meaning in his words "so marry such of the women as seem good to you": his words "such of the women as seem good to you" admit of the meaning "such as you desire"; and it may be that what is meant is "such as are lawful for you"; and it may be that what is meant is "such as are easy for you". all of that is possible. but we came to know by other evidence that what is meant is "such as have been made lawful for you", and that is what "seems good". [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: A Letter on the Merit of the Ten Days of Dhu al-Hijjah
a: رسالة في فضل عشر ذي الحجة
b:
from muhammad al-hasan ibn al-dedew, to every muslim whom this reaches. peace be upon you, and the mercy of god and his blessings.

to proceed: among the best seasons of good in the year is this season with which god has favoured you, in these excellent days, which are the best days of the year. the group of collectors (al-jamāʿah), except muslim and al-nasa’i, transmitted from the hadith of ibn abbas (may god be pleased with them both), who said: the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace) said: "there are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to god, mighty and majestic, than these days" — meaning the ten of dhu al-hijjah. and ahmad and others transmitted from the hadith of ibn umar (may god be pleased with them both), who said: the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace) said: "there are no days greater in god’s sight, glorified be he, nor in which deeds are more beloved to him, than these ten days; so increase in them the declaration of god’s oneness, the magnification of god and the praise of god."

so strive in righteous deeds during these days, and especially in the following:

1 — fasting all of them. ahmad and al-nasa’i transmitted from hafsah bint umar (may god be pleased with them both), who said: "four things the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace) did not leave: fasting ʿāshurāʾ, and the ten, and three days of every month, and the two units of prayer before the morning prayer." what is meant is other than the day of eid, for it is not lawful to fast it. that is why abu dawud transmitted from one of the wives of the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace), who said: "the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) used to fast the nine of dhu al-hijjah, and the day of ʿāshurāʾ, and three days of every month, and the first monday of the month, and thursday." as for aishah’s hadith in muslim, "i never saw the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace) fasting during the ten at all" — it is to be understood as referring to the hajj.

2 — fasting the day of arafah in particular, for one who is not performing the hajj. muslim, ahmad, abu dawud and ibn majah transmitted from abu qatadah (may god be pleased with him), who said: the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace) said: "fasting the day of arafah expiates two years, one past and one to come; and fasting the day of ʿāshurāʾ expiates one past year." in another wording: "i reckon upon god that it expiates the year before it and the year after it."

3 — abundant remembrance of god. al-bukhari said in the ṣaḥīḥ: "ibn abbas said: {and that they may mention the name of god on appointed days} (sūrat al-ḥajj 22:28) — the days of the ten. he said: ibn umar and abu hurayrah used to go out to the market during the days of the ten, magnifying god, and the people would magnify god at their magnification." and there has already come, in the hadith of ibn umar, the command to increase the declaration of god’s oneness, the magnification of god and the praise of god.

4 — that the one intending to offer the sacrifice should not take anything from his hair or his nails from the beginning of the month until he sacrifices, in resemblance to the one in the consecrated state of pilgrimage (iḥrām). the group of collectors, except al-bukhari, transmitted from the hadith of umm salamah (may god be pleased with her) that the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace) said: "whoever has an animal to slaughter — when the crescent of dhu al-hijjah appears, let him not take anything from his hair or his nails until he sacrifices."

may god grant us and you success in every good, and accept from us and from you.

written by muhammad al-hasan ibn al-dedew — may god be his protector and helper. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: The Established Supplication in the Prayer over the Deceased
a: الدعاء الثابت في الصلاة على الميت
b:
question: what is the established supplication in the prayer over the deceased, and what is the authenticity of the supplication called the supplication of abu hurayrah (may god be pleased with him)?

answer: many hadiths have come concerning the supplication in the funeral prayer. the supplication he asked about, which is attributed to abu hurayrah (may god be pleased with him), is a report stopping at a companion (mawqūf): it is established from abu hurayrah, but he did not trace it up to the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). as for the reports traced to the prophet (marfūʿ), among them is his saying (peace and blessings be upon him):

"o god, forgive our living and our dead, our present and our absent, our elder and our younger, our male and our female. you know our comings and our goings. o god, whomever of us you keep alive, keep him alive upon islam; and whomever of us you cause to die, cause him to die upon faith. o god, forgive this deceased and have mercy on him, grant him well-being and pardon him, and shelter him from the trial of the grave, from the punishment of the grave and from the punishment of the fire. o god, if he was a doer of good, increase him in his good; and if he was a wrongdoer, pass over his misdeeds. o god, do not deprive us of his reward and do not put us to trial after him, and forgive us and him."

and there are other hadiths to the same effect: "o god, our companion has descended upon you, and you are the most generous upon whom one may descend. o god, so make his lodging generous, widen his place of entry, and give him in exchange a home better than his home, a family better than his family and a spouse better than his spouse; wash him with water, snow and hail, and cleanse him of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt." and there are yet other hadiths besides these.

t: Patience Under Trial
a: الصبر علي الابتلاء
b:
praise belongs to god; we praise him and seek his help, and we take refuge with god from the evils of our souls and from the ill consequences of our deeds. whomever god guides, none can lead astray; and whomever he leads astray, none can guide. i bear witness that there is no god but god alone, having no partner; and i bear witness that muhammad is his servant and messenger — may god bless him and his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace.

{o mankind, be conscious of your lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate, and from the two of them spread abroad many men and women. and be conscious of god, through whom you ask of one another, and of the ties of kinship. indeed god is ever watchful over you} (sūrat al-nisāʾ 4:1).

{o you who believe, be conscious of god and speak a word that is apt: he will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. and whoever obeys god and his messenger has attained a great triumph} (sūrat al-aḥzāb 33:70–71).

to proceed: the best of speech is the book of god, and the best guidance is the guidance of muhammad (may god bless him and grant him peace); the worst of matters are those newly invented, and every innovation in religion (bidʿah) is a going astray.

servants of god, god, glorified and exalted, tries his servants with good and with evil, so that he may know which of them is best in deed — and he knows that already, for he is the one who knows the outcomes of affairs and where they lead, and everything has its end with him. he, glorified and exalted, sent the messengers with the criterion, in order to distinguish between people. for people were one community until god sent the prophets, and they divided people: a party to the garden and a party to the blaze. god, be he exalted, said: {mankind was one community; then god sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and as warners, and sent down with them the book} (sūrat al-baqarah 2:213). this book which the prophets brought from god, mighty and majestic, is what divides people into two camps: a camp of good in which there is no evil, and a camp of evil in which there is no good; and by it people are distinguished along the path of guidance.

god, be he exalted, is free of need of all his servants. he tries them by that only by way of sifting and purifying, and he chooses from among them his party and his friends, whom he prepares so that he may whiten their faces on the day when faces are whitened and faces are blackened; and that he may give them their books in their right hands, before their faces; and that he may grant them the highest firdaws of the garden, beneath the throne of the most merciful.

he, glorified and exalted, has made that an unchanging pattern (sunnah) upon which the course of this whole universe runs, from the descent of adam and eve to this earth until god inherits the earth and those upon it. among these patterns god has made the pattern of the mutual repelling between truth and falsehood; and it is an unchanging pattern upon this earth — were it to cease, the benefits of the people of the earth would be wholly disrupted: {and were it not for god’s repelling people, some by means of others, the earth would be corrupted} (sūrat al-baqarah 2:251).

for that reason, the friends of god, mighty and majestic, who desire to look upon his noble face and to dwell in the gardens of bliss, must be patient for the sake of their lord, mighty and majestic; for he said to his messenger (may god bless him and grant him peace): "and for your lord, be patient" (sūrat al-muddaththir 74:7).

then they must know that when god, glorified and exalted, tests a servant and tries him, what counts is the outcome of the matter. for he has decreed, in all the revealed books, victory for his friends, and this victory cannot fail. god, be he exalted, said in the warning given by moses (peace be upon him): {indeed the earth belongs to god; he causes to inherit it whom he wills of his servants, and the outcome belongs to the god-conscious} (sūrat al-aʿrāf 7:128) — and that was when the companions of moses complained to him: {they said: we were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us. he said: perhaps your lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the earth, and then see how you act} (sūrat al-aʿrāf 7:129). he had already informed them of this unchanging pattern: {indeed the earth belongs to god; he causes to inherit it whom he wills of his servants, and the outcome belongs to the god-conscious}.

he made that clear in the warning given by david, saying: {and we have written in the psalms, after the reminder, that the earth shall be inherited by my righteous servants. indeed in this is a message for a people who worship} (sūrat al-anbiyāʾ 21:105–106).

and he made it clear in the warning given by muhammad (may god bless him and grant him peace), for he, be he exalted, said: {permission is given to those who are fought against, because they have been wronged — and indeed god is able to give them victory: those who have been driven from their homes without right, only because they said, "our lord is god." and were it not for god’s repelling of people, some by means of others, there would surely have been demolished cloisters and churches and synagogues and mosques in which the name of god is much mentioned. and god will surely help those who help him; indeed god is strong, mighty. those who, if we establish them in the land, perform the prayer and give zakat, and enjoin right and forbid wrong. and to god belongs the outcome of all affairs} (sūrat al-ḥajj 22:39–41).

this verse is explicit that god, glorified and exalted, repels by his friends the scheming of his enemies, and makes that an unchanging pattern. were it not for this repelling, there would have been demolished cloisters and churches and synagogues and mosques in which the name of god is much mentioned. were it not for the repelling of god’s enemies by his friends, the m

t: The Source of the Muslim’s Honour
a: مصدر عزة المسلم
b:
in the name of god, the most merciful, the most compassionate. praise be to god, lord of the worlds. i invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his companions, and upon whoever is guided by his guidance and takes his sunnah as his way until the day of judgement.

to proceed: god has made man by nature a lover of honour (ʿizzah), so that he strives to attain it by every path and by every means. but this honour has causes that lead to it, and it is not attained without them; and many people search for it where it does not lie and seek it where it is not to be sought. the generality of those who seek honour seek it through the affairs of this passing world — through the authority and the instruments of overwhelming power it contains, and likewise through dominion, numbers, wealth and the like. none of these is a cause of honour. god, be he exalted, made that clear in his book explicitly, in his words: {do they seek honour with them? indeed honour belongs entirely to god} (sūrat al-nisāʾ 4:139). so all honour belongs to god, glorified and exalted; and the creature attains honour only by connection with the creator, glorified and exalted, by depending upon him and by relying upon him, glorified and exalted, alone. for this reason god, be he exalted, said: {and to god belongs honour, and to his messenger and to the believers; but the hypocrites do not know} (sūrat al-munāfiqūn 63:8).

t: Urging Attendance at the Dawn Prayer in the Mosque
a: الحض على صلاة الصبح في المسجد
b:
question: what do you advise someone who always misses the dawn prayer in congregation?

answer: this person should remember that it is the prayer of the hypocrites, and that the companions of the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recognise a man’s hypocrisy by his absence from the congregation at the dawn prayer: if he did not attend the evening prayer and the dawn prayer in congregation (jamāʿah), they judged him to be a hypocrite and knew that he was one of the hypocrites.

therefore we must be diligent in performing it in congregation, and must know that whoever performs these two prayers in congregation is under god’s protection — so let god not call you to account for anything of his protection. and whoever performs them both in congregation has recorded for him the standing of a night and half a night. so a person must be diligent, especially when he knows that the reward for walking in darkness to the dawn prayer is perfect light on the day of resurrection: "give glad tidings to those who walk much through the darkness of night to the mosques, of perfect light on the day of resurrection."

therefore we must all be diligent, young and old, in attending the dawn prayer in congregation, and must remember the words of god, be he exalted: {and the qur’an of the dawn — indeed the qur’an of the dawn is witnessed} (sūrat al-isrāʾ 17:78). it is witnessed: two kinds of angels witness it, the angels of the night and the angels of the day: "angels take turns among you, angels by night and angels by day, and they gather at the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer." [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: The Ruling on Seeking a Means of Approach to God (Tawassul)
a: حكم التوسل
b:
question: i submitted to one of the sheikhs a request for [admission to] his spiritual path (ṭarīqah), and he granted it to me accompanied by conditions, among them: taking it in earnest, the covenant and secrecy, and that i not breach the condition, nor the oneness of god (tawḥīd), nor the obligatory duties. i am without religious learning, so i remained on that path and in the service of the sheikh until he died. i then became accustomed to visiting [his grave] with reverence and supplication; and after that i seek a means of approach to god (tawassul) through his righteous deeds, just as i used to seek a means of approach through him while he was alive, in order to obtain benefits and to remove harms. is this part of the sunnah, or is it associating partners with god (shirk) — may god protect us?

answer: these counsels which the sheikh gave him are unobjectionable. a person must take [his religion] in earnest, must fulfil the covenant, must likewise not breach the oneness of god nor the obligatory duties, and must learn religious knowledge. these are counsels which the sheikh is obliged to give, and the one counselled is likewise obliged to receive always; for the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) said: "the religion is sincere counsel. we said: to whom? he said: to god, to his book, to his messenger, to the leaders of the muslims and to their generality."

as for what he mentioned, that he is without religious learning: the mere formulae of remembrance (dhikr) which he performs do not dispense with the seeking of knowledge. rather a person is bound to learn what the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) brought — for perhaps what he is doing is in the first place contrary to what the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) brought. so let him search out what the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) brought, and act upon it, and make it the judge over everything else. if what the sheikh or anyone else commanded him agrees with what the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) brought, then let a person act upon it, because the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) commanded it. and if it is contrary to something the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) brought, then let him return it to whoever said it, whoever that may be; and let him not be ashamed to reject from anyone anything that contradicts what the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) brought — even if he be a father, or a sheikh, or an elder. it is not possible for you to accept from anyone at all what is contrary to what the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) brought.

as for what this person does after the death of the aforementioned sheikh, in the way of visiting [the grave]: visiting graves is recommended (mandūb) in general for muslims, in order to call the hereafter to mind. but the one visited derives no benefit from it, does not perceive it, does not sense it at all, and hears nothing of what the visitor says; nor can he benefit him with anything — he can neither remove a harm from him nor bring him a benefit, and there is no relationship at all between the two. rather you take admonition from his bones, which the earth consumes; and you take admonition from his secrets and his wealth, which have become the property of others; and you take admonition from his family, who used to think that he benefited them and looked after their affairs, and now he has departed from them and has not harmed them in anything. this is what you obtain from visiting any grave. visiting graves — whether their occupants be people of faith or people of unbelief, people of righteousness or people of corruption, whether you know them or do not know them — leads to this calling to mind, the calling to mind of the hereafter; and this is what is sought from it.

as for the dead, they benefit in their graves only by supplication — that you supplicate for them. and if you supplicate for them, whether you are with them at their graves or outside, they do not hear, but they benefit, and there is no difference: the supplication reaches [them] whether from near or from far, by night or by day, in whatever place you are.

as for the innovated visiting which people perform — going to graves, speaking at them, frequenting them, standing over the tombs, and even raising their needs to them — there is no doubt that this is manifest associating of partners with god (shirk). and of the same [category] is seeking a means of approach through the deeds of other persons: this is not permissible for you. it is permissible for you only to seek a means of approach through your own deeds, because you are asking god by something you yourself have offered; for you cannot seek a means of approach to him by the deed of another person, which that person himself deserves — for it is the doer who is paid his wage in full. every person may seek a means of approach by a deed which he himself performed and in which he was sincere to god; but he can never seek a means of approach by the deed of another person.

so this brother must repent to god for what has passed; must abandon seeking a means of approach through the deeds of other persons which he himself did not perform; must keep to earnestness and the covenant as he was commanded, and to the oneness of god and the obligatory duties; and must learn religious knowledge. this is better for him, and this is what accords with the sunnah of the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace).

(and in general, tawassul belongs properly to jurisprudence (fiqh) and not to creed.)

t: The Completed Qur’an Recitation on Behalf of the Deceased
a: الختمة للميت
b:
question: is the completed recitation of the qur’an (khatmah) for the deceased permissible or not — the one that is called al-salkah?

answer: whether the reward of the qur’an reaches the deceased after his death is a point of disagreement among the people of knowledge. the school of malik and of al-shafi’i is that it does not reach [him], on the ground that the governing principle is the words of god, be he exalted: {or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of moses, and of abraham who fulfilled [his covenant] — that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that man shall have nothing but what he strove for, and that his striving shall be seen, and then he shall be repaid for it with the fullest repayment} (sūrat al-najm 53:36–41). on this principle, this act does not reach [him] after death.

as for abu hanifa and ahmad, they held that it does reach [him], by analogy (qiyās) of the recitation of the qur’an upon voluntary charity (ṣadaqah), the hajj, the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah) and other kinds of pious act. it is agreed that voluntary charity and supplication reach [the deceased] definitively, and everything apart from those two falls within the disagreement — because for voluntary charity and supplication, sound hadiths from the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) are established; and likewise for the hajj and the lesser pilgrimage, sound hadiths are established. as for everything else, no explicit text (naṣṣ) from the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) has come concerning it. and the disagreement remains: is this among the fixed quantities (al-muqaddarāt) into which analogy does not enter, or is it not among the fixed quantities, so that analogy is possible in it? this is a point of disagreement in legal theory (uṣūl) which cannot be settled.

on this basis, those who perform the completed recitation following a person’s death and wish to convey it to him — the more cautious and the better course for them is to give voluntary charity on his behalf and to supplicate for him, for this is what reaches [him] without any disagreement. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: The Ruling on Praying in a Mosque Built on Land Not Lawfully Allocated
a: حكم الصلاة في مسجد أقيم في مكان غير مشرع
b:
question: some of the imams last friday say that prayer in this mosque is not valid, because it is makzūr [built on land taken by al-kazrah]?

answer: mosques do not fall within the scope of what is called al-kazrah. we have already mentioned that al-kazrah is bringing land into use by force — that is, taking ownership by force, without permission. mosques are the common property of the people; they are not personal property. hence they do not fall within that. they belong to god, glorified and exalted; he has freed them from the ownership of [his] servants and from the ownership of others, so they do not fall into this category at all.

t: Incantations and Amulets
a: الرقى والتمائم
b:
question: a woman asks about the folk illness (al-sall al-maṣṣ). she has a ram’s horn in which there is a black ḥikmah, and with it a tizlūmīt. the horn is placed in water which the person afflicted with al-sall drinks, and he is cured by god’s leave; as for the tizlūmīt, it is used for a woman whose post-natal bleeding has become difficult. what is the ruling of the sharia on that, bearing in mind that she uses it for the benefit of the muslims, and that she knows it neither harms nor benefits except by god’s leave?

answer: these incantations are of long standing and were among the practices of the pre-islamic age. the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "present your incantations to me." whatever among them contained magnification of god and remembrance of him, the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) approved; and whatever was other than that, he rejected and forbade. so everything whose meaning a person does not know, it is not permissible for him to use as an incantation.

as for these physical objects, such as horns and what is called tizlūmīt and the like, it is not permissible to use them, because a person does not know what is in them; and if he does know, then they are things whose outward form is like the outward form of sorcery, since they are physical objects and matters of that kind. for this reason this type harms and does not benefit. and what is observed of immediate benefit from it — such as recovery from some illness — is only a trial, because a person will become attached to it and will suppose that it heals or benefits; so it is a trial by which god tries [people].

we are now awaiting the dajjal, so we must beware of matters such as these. if a person is to beware of the trial of the false messiah, let him know that the dajjal revives the dead: he calls them and they rise from their graves. he passes by the ruined village and its treasures follow him like swarms of bees. he comes to the people of a village who are in drought and in the utmost hardship, and they believe him, so he commands the sky and it rains, and commands the earth and it brings forth growth, and their livestock return to them with the fattest udders they have ever had. and he passes by the people of a village who are in plenty and they deny him, so he commands the sky and it withholds, and commands the earth and it becomes parched, and their livestock return to them in the severest distress.

so if we know this, and know that these worldly observable phenomena are only trials which god, be he exalted, brings about — just as he brings about more severe ones at the hand of the false messiah — then a person must not be deceived by them, and must know that trials exist; and that a person’s following them blindly, and his testifying that the matter is merely a thing observed — that so-and-so drank this and was cured, and it was hung upon such-and-such a woman and she was cured — this type is only among the trials which a person must beware of. for if everyone who cured a sick person were to be followed, the dajjal would have the better claim to this, since he revives the dead.

therefore one must be on the utmost guard against this type, and against its doctrinal danger, which affects people’s creed. and let us know that god, glorified and exalted, has given us that in which there is healing and light. he sent down upon us this clear qur’an, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, a revelation from one wise, praiseworthy. it is god’s firm rope and his straight path: whoever holds fast to it is protected, and whoever abandons it, of any tyrant, god breaks his back. god, be he exalted, said: {and we send down of the qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers} (sūrat al-isrāʾ 17:82). and he said: {and when you recite the qur’an, we place between you and those who do not believe in the hereafter a concealed veil; and we place coverings over their hearts lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness. and when you mention your lord alone in the qur’an, they turn their backs in aversion} (sūrat al-isrāʾ 17:45–46). and he, be he exalted, said: {and if there were a qur’an by which the mountains were moved, or the earth were cloven asunder, or the dead were spoken to — nay, but to god belongs the whole affair} (sūrat al-raʿd 13:31).

for this reason we must content ourselves with the book of god, be he exalted, and seek guidance in it, and beware of these distractions that distract from it. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: The Difference Between Islam and Faith
a: الفرق بين الإسلام والإيمان
b:
question: the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) explained faith (īmān) in the hadith of the delegation of abd al-qays in the same terms in which he explained islam in the hadith of gabriel. how are the two explanations to be reconciled?

answer: faith and islam are two sharia terms: when they come together they diverge, and when they come apart they converge. so if they occur in a single context, their meanings differ, as in the hadith of gabriel; and if they occur in two different contexts, their meanings are one and the same, as in the hadith of the delegation of abd al-qays.

for in the hadith of the delegation of abd al-qays, when they said to the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him), "we can reach you only in the sacred month, and between us and you lies this clan of the disbelievers of mudar; so command us with a decisive command by which we may act, of which we may inform those we have left behind, and by which we may enter paradise" — he commanded them four things and forbade them four things. he said: "i command you to believe in god alone. do you know what belief in god alone is?" and he explained to them belief in god alone as: that they bear witness that there is no god but god and that muhammad is the messenger of god, that they establish the prayer, and that they hand over a fifth of the spoils. and he made clear to them the four drinks which they were to leave. so he explained to them the concept of faith by part of the concept of islam — which indicates that when faith and islam occur separately their meanings are one and the same.

but when they occur in a single context — as in the verse of sūrat al-ḥujurāt, which is the words of god, be he exalted: {the bedouin say, "we believe." say: you do not believe; rather say, "we have submitted"} (sūrat al-ḥujurāt 49:14) — then their meanings differ, as in the hadith of gabriel. likewise the hadith of sa’d ibn abi waqqas in the two ṣaḥīḥs: that the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) gave to certain men and left out one man who was the most pleasing of them to me; and what i knew of him overcame me, so i said: "o messenger of god, what is the matter with you regarding so-and-so? by god, i regard him as a believer." he said: "or a muslim?" so the messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) distinguished between the two words when they occurred in a single context. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: Distinguishing the Marks of Divine Honour Given to God’s Friends from Other Extraordinary Events
a: الفرق بين كرامة الأولياء وغيرها
b:
question: there are breaks in the natural order, some of which are a mark of divine honour (karāmah) from god, glorified and exalted, for his friends, and some of which are satanic. how do we distinguish between them?

answer: one distinguishes between them only by the state of the person himself. whoever is committed to the sharia, conforming outwardly and inwardly to god’s law — what he attains of that is a mark of honour with which god has honoured him. and whoever is opposed to the sharia, disobedient and an innovator — what he attains of that is from satan, or is a trial and a test from god, be he exalted.

t: Books That Should Be Attended To for Understanding Sound Creed
a: الكتب التي ينبغي الإعتناء بها من حيث الفهم للعقيدة الصحيحة
b:
question: which books do you direct us to, that should be attended to for understanding sound creed (ʿaqīdah)? may god reward you well.

answer: the books which the righteous predecessors composed in this field contain sufficiency for the muslims. among these books, for example, are the book of faith (kitāb al-īmān) of abu bakr ibn abi shaybah; the book of faith of abu khaythamah zuhayr ibn harb, the teacher of muslim; and likewise al-bukhari’s book (may god have mercy on him) the creation of the acts of servants (khalq afʿāl al-ʿibād); and likewise the book of al-lalaka’i, the exposition of the foundations of the sunnah (sharḥ uṣūl al-sunnah). these books are beneficial and important.

t: On the Claim by Some of the Living to Meet the Dead
a: الكلام على ادعاء بعض الأحياء للقاء الأموات
b:
question: what is your comment on someone who claims to meet the dead, and to know which of them are people of paradise and which of the fire, and the like?

answer: the state of the dead, beyond the intermediate realm (barzakh) that lies before them until the day of resurrection, is among the unseen matters upon which we are not informed except by revelation. a person may be made aware, by way of an imaginative apprehension (takhyīl) or the like, or at times by hearing, of the punishment of the dead in their graves; but that may be cut off from them, and they may then be in bliss. so this is among the matters that do not entail certainty.

the companions of the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) were with him one night and heard terrifying sounds, and he said: "that is the jews being punished in their graves." he made clear to them that this was the punishment of the grave — the punishment of the banu qurayzah whom the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) had put to death; they were being punished in their graves, and his companions heard their voices. this is an unseen matter which god disclosed to them at that time, so that they might increase in awe of god and in reliance upon him.

likewise, ibn umar went out on a journey alone in the time of the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and passed by a grave, and its occupant came out to him from his grave, saying: "o abd allah, give me to drink." he said: "i did not know whether he knew my name, or whether it is a phrase the arabs use." then something came out after him and dragged him back violently and said: "o abd allah, do not give him to drink." and abd allah developed a fever — that is, he was struck with the shivering fever, which is a severe fever. so the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade travelling alone because of that.

the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) made clear some of the states of the people of the graves in their graves, for he hears from them what we do not hear, and sees it: he sees the punishment of the grave and sees its bliss — but that is by revelation, as is soundly established from him in the two ṣaḥīḥs, that he passed by two fresh graves and said: "indeed these two are being punished, and they are not being punished for anything great." then he said: "rather — as for one of them, he did not shield himself from urine; and as for the other, he used to go about with tale-bearing." likewise he said: "these graves are darkness upon their occupants, and god illuminates them by my prayer and my supplication." and he informed [us] of the places of trials and of other matters connected with the punishment of the grave — all of that by way of revelation.

for this reason no one can claim such a thing, unless he has heard sounds by way of an imaginative apprehension, as happened to the companions. that indicates that at that moment the sound issuing may be from the punishment of the grave, and then it passes away. for the punishment of the grave is not a perpetual punishment like the punishment of the hereafter; it is not like the punishment of the disbelievers in the fire, but rather it ceases. a person may be punished for some moments, and then it is cut off from him.

and the punishment of the grave is among the expiators of sins — it is counted among the expiators of sins; because if a person deserves a punishment in return for one of his sins, and that punishment is brought forward for him in the grave, he is raised on the day of resurrection without that sin upon him, and so deserves paradise without punishment. the erudite scholar sayyid abd allah ibn al-hajj ibrahim counted it among the expiators of sins, and some of the people of knowledge before him counted it likewise.
