t: On the Division of This Ummah into Sects
a: الكلام على افتراق هذه الأمة
b:
question: do the sects which the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned in the hadith abide eternally in the fire, and is there any way for the people of the sunnah to be united with them?

answer: the prophet’s (peace and blessings be upon him) saying, "the jews split into seventy-one sects, the christians split into seventy-two sects, and my ummah will split into seventy-three sects" — this much of the hadith is sound (ṣaḥīḥ); al-hakim and others transmitted it, and it is sound through its various narrations. as for the addition — "all of them in the fire except one", or "all of them in paradise except one", or "whoever is upon the like of what i and my companions are upon" — none of these additions is sound. so the sound hadith is only the affirmation of the division, and it is one of the signs of prophethood and one of its proofs; but that they are in the fire, or in paradise, or that it is what he and his companions were upon — none of this is soundly established from the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him).

as for the sects within this ummah: whatever among them is innovation (ibtidāʿ) and error in religion, its adherent not being an unbeliever thereby — then whoever dies bearing witness that there is no god but god and that muhammad is the messenger of god does not abide eternally in the fire, even if he was in error, even if he was an innovator, however great his disobedience. rather god, glorified and exalted, will either pass over him, or punish him to the measure of his disobedience and then bring him out of the fire. for god, be he exalted, brings out of the fire on the day of resurrection peoples who have turned black and been scorched, and they are cast into the river of life, and their bodies grow as the seed grows in the silt carried by a torrent; then they enter paradise. and they may also be punished in their graves — and the punishment of the grave is among the expiators of sins, by which sins are lightened — so that when they are raised on the day of resurrection they will already have received the recompense of their innovation and their error.

as for those who innovated innovations that constitute unbelief, they are few — praise be to god — and the ummah has cast them out; they have been tried and judged against, fought and killed. those still have followers in every age and in every time; but most of them, praise be to god, do not ascribe themselves to the sunnah.

t: On Interpretation (Taʾwīl)
a: الكلام على التأويل
b:
question: is the default position the absence of interpretation (taʾwīl), or is the default interpretation? and what is the authenticity of ibn abbas’s statement on the interpretation of {and your lord comes, and the angels rank upon rank} (sūrat al-fajr 89:22)?

answer: if the question concerns the interpretation of the attributes of the creator, glorified and exalted, then the basis for interpreting them is only fear of likening him to his creation — this is what drives it in the first place. but the reality is that we have no need of it at all. for whoever believes in god and in what his messenger brought from him, and knows that no one knows god better than god, and that after that no one knows god better than the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him); and knows that the messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is the trustworthy counsellor, eager for the guidance of the ummah — he would not have left them in confusion and loss, and would not have brought them what suggests likening [god to creation] or suggests error, and then kept silent until he died and met god without having explained that to his ummah and without having made it clear to them!

do you know anyone who gives people more sincere counsel than the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him)? do you think anyone is more solicitous for people’s creed than the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him)? why would the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) leave that interpretation, and then other peoples come along and interpret? the messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is the most sincere of people towards people, and he is the one solicitous for them, as our lord, glorified and exalted, informed [us] and testified for him, saying: {there has come to you a messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is your suffering; anxious is he over you; to the believers kind and merciful} (sūrat al-tawbah 9:128).

for this reason it is said to whoever wants that position: this to which you call — did the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) call to it, and abu bakr and umar and uthman and ali, or did they not call to it? if he admits that they did not call to it, it is said: then from where do you have knowledge of it? and from where do you have [the warrant] to call to it, when those did not call to it? this is the silencing answer in the case of those people. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: On Fortune-Telling and Geomancy
a: الكلام على العِرافة والضرب في الرمل
b:
question: this question is about the ruling on al-gāzānah, and whether those who practise it are among the fortune-tellers (ʿarrāfūn), and whether the one who does that is sinful or not.

answer: what people call al-gāzānah is geomancy — "striking in the sand" (al-ḍarb fī al-raml). the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked about striking in the sand, and he mentioned that one of god’s prophets used to draw lines; so whoever’s line coincides with his, that is it — and otherwise there is no good in it.

it is of two categories. the first is what involves seeking to look upon unseen matters and asserting them with certainty. this is definitively forbidden (ḥarām); no prophet did it; and it falls within the scope of fortune-telling (ʿirāfah). the second kind is what is not like that, but consists rather of inferring from signs, as god, be he exalted, said: {and landmarks; and by the star they are guided} (sūrat al-naḥl 16:16) — as when a person infers that rain will fall from his seeing a rain-bearing constellation or lightning, for example; or infers that grapes or dates are ripe from the ripening of some of them. this kind is among the matters referred back to the ruling of custom (ʿurf), and the people of knowledge differ concerning it. some of them held that this is astrology, even if it is ascribed to secondary causes, and held it forbidden. others held that it is not astrology, and that it is an ascription of effects to their causes — and the ascription of effects to causes has come in a number of sharia texts.

sheikh abd al-qadir ibn muhammad ibn muhammad salim (may god’s mercy be upon them all) versified this disagreement, saying:

*if the practitioner of astrology is a believer in god, and does not ascribe effect at all to the star, and holds that god has made a star a sign of some event brought about by god — then he is a wrongdoer, and one whose standing is impugned until he repents; and it is not permissible for one who follows the sharia to follow him, in the view of the discerning. ibn farhun the imam ascribed it to a unique figure, renowned for mastering the questions and for understanding — abu dalaf, the illustrious one of the world, their ibn rushd — from the well-pleasing master sahnun, the man of understanding. yet al-mazari allowed this, on the strength of his saying — upon him be god’s peace in the beginning and at the end — "when a cloud arises from the direction of the sea", which is apparent [in meaning]; and there has come concerning it what indicates this ruling.*

al-mazari holds that this is permissible, and adduces as evidence the report transmitted without a complete chain (balāgh) which malik recorded in the muwaṭṭaʾ — one of the four balāghāt which abu umar did not connect in al-tamhīd, and which ibn al-salah did connect. this balāgh states that the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "when a baḥriyyah arises and then turns towards syria, that is a spring of abundant water." "when a baḥriyyah arises" — that is, when the rain-cloud appears from the direction of the sea, that is, from the west relative to medina; "then turns towards syria" — that is, heads north; "that is a spring of abundant water" — that is, plentiful in water: much rain comes from it. most of medina’s rain comes from the direction of the west, and especially when it heads northwards. this is a ruling drawn from custom, and it is evidence for the permissibility of relying upon customary signs in such matters.

ibn rushd narrated from sahnun the prohibition of that, because he placed it within the scope of the astrology which the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade.

therefore, if the gāzān is among those who ascribe effect to created things, or who seek to look upon unseen matters, then he is a fortune-teller: it is not permissible to believe him, nor to come to him at all — even if a person does not believe him; and no prayer of his is accepted for forty days if he comes to him, or believes him in what he says. but if he is among those who infer only by physiognomic discernment and by signs, and does not assert it with certainty, then that has a basis; for god, be he exalted, said: {and landmarks; and by the star they are guided} (sūrat al-naḥl 16:16), and he, be he exalted, said: {… signs for those who discern} (sūrat al-ḥijr 15:75). those who discern are the people of insight, who distinguish matters and connect pieces of information until they arrive at certain non-definitive conclusions, forming opinions about them which may be confirmed and may not be confirmed — like dream-visions, which give pleasure but do not delude. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: On Obsessive Misgivings in Ritual Purity and Prayer, and the Ways of Treating Them
a: الكلام على الوسوسة في الطهارة والصلاة وطرق علاجها
b:
question: i have a son who is seized by obsessive misgivings (waswasah) in ritual purity (ṭahārah) and in prayer. when he goes to the lavatory and purifies himself from urine, he performs ablution (wuḍūʾ) until he finishes, and then says: "i have not finished with the urine, and i cannot pray with substantive impurity (najāsah)" — and he takes off all his clothes and takes other clothes and prays.

answer: this kind is from the work of satan. god, be he exalted, said: {o you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of satan} (sūrat al-nūr 24:21). so he must treat himself for this illness by the sharia means of healing. among them: frequent seeking of forgiveness; likewise the formulae of remembrance for entering and leaving the lavatory, and keeping to them; likewise not wearying himself by thinking a great deal about this matter — he is obliged to turn it away from himself; likewise the sharia-sanctioned recitation (al-ruqyah al-sharʿiyyah), that he recite the qur’an over himself and that another recite it over him; likewise keeping to the formulae of remembrance for sleeping, for waking, and for morning and evening; and likewise voluntary charity (ṣadaqah), by which illness is treated — "treat your sick with voluntary charity." all of that will remove this obsessive misgiving from him, by god’s leave. [translator's note: renderings of qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the arabic.]

t: On Breaks in the Natural Order
a: الكلام على خوارق العادات
b:
question: what appears of extraordinary events at the hand of the friend of god (walī), and what appears at the hand of the sorcerer — what is the difference between them?

answer: the people of knowledge mentioned that breaks in the natural order are of seven categories: four of them for good and three for evil.

the four that are for good are, first, the portents (irhāṣāt) which appear at the birth of the prophets and in their childhood — such as the cracking of chosroes’ palace hall, the extinguishing of the fire of the persians, what halimah witnessed of extraordinary events in the childhood of the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), the splitting of his breast and the like. these are not miracles (muʿjizāt) but portents, and they point to his being sent; for at that time he had not yet been sent — he was sent at the head of forty years.

the second kind is the evidentiary miracles (muʿjizāt): what appears at the hand of the prophets at the moment of challenge, in conveying the messages of their lord — such as the descent of revelation, the ascension and the night journey, the splitting of the moon and the like, and the she-camel of salih and the staff of moses. this is the evidentiary miracle, and it is particular to the prophets.

the third category is what is called the marks of divine honour given to god’s friends (karāmāt al-awliyāʾ): what god bestows upon one who is of the people of obedience, god-consciousness (taqwā) and faith, of what assists him in obedience — such as bodily strength, so that a person is able to persevere in ablution (wuḍūʾ) and the full ritual washing. this is a mark of honour with which god honours his friends. likewise keeping to the first row, or to answering the caller to prayer, or to prayer in congregation, or to completing the qur’an every day and night, for example, or keeping to the night vigil throughout the year. this is a mark of honour with which god honours whom he wills of his friends, and it is a break in the custom of the generality of people. this type is called the marks of honour, and most of them are not directed to this world but to the matters of the hereafter. for the marks of honour in most cases are not directed to worldly matters — as that a person should find money, or a car, or a telephone, or the like. these are trivial worldly matters, and god’s honouring of his servants relates to things greater than this, such as his honouring his friends with what helps them in his worship and his obedience, and what increases them in faith, awe and god-consciousness.

the fourth kind is what is called aid (ʿawn): what is attained by the middling among the muslims, those not renowned for obedience or for worship, for whom god appoints some extraordinary matter on account of their faith — as one whose mount bolted from him in an empty stretch of land and a tree held it for him. this kind, which assists in worldly matters, does not fall within the scope of the mark of honour; rather it is aid by which god aids his servants, appointing for them what helps them in the matters of their world, which is a break in the natural order.

these four are for good. as for the three that are for evil:

the first is what is called humiliation (ihānah): what appears of extraordinary events at the hand of a false claimant to prophethood, contrary to his claim. musaylimah the liar heard that the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) wiped the head of a boy and he did not go grey — his hair stayed black until he died an old man; so musaylimah wiped the head of a boy and he went bald. and he heard that the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) spat into a well that was salty and it became sweet; so he spat into a well and it dried up. this kind is called humiliation. it is truly a break in the natural order — this is extraordinary — but it is a humiliation, because it is not in the manner sought and is the opposite of the manner the person seeks.

the second kind of these extraordinary events that are for evil is sorcery (siḥr). sorcery is what has already been defined, in its two categories: what is illusion and what is [real] effect. by it a break in the natural order occurs, and it is for evil; it is unbelief on the part of the one who practises it.

the third kind of the extraordinary events that are for evil is what is called soothsaying (kahānah) and consorting with the jinn. the jinn break the natural order for a person: they hear a single word from the unseen and add to it ninety-nine lies, and bring him a hundred words containing one word of truth and ninety-nine lies. he then reports what they reported to him, so that sometimes a truthful one comes to him and sometimes a lying one. as saf ibn sayyad said to the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) when he asked him, as is in the ṣaḥīḥ: he said, "what comes to you, o saf?" he said, "there comes to me a truthful one and a lying one." he said, "be off — you will never exceed your measure." so the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) knew that what came to him was from satan, because what is from god contains no liar — it must necessarily be truthful. so he said, "there comes to me a truthful one and a lying one", and he said, "be off — you will never exceed your measure."

these, then, are the breaks in the natural order; their categories are clear and the distinction between them is plain. what causes difficulty for some people is only what occurs to some of god’s friends of reporting certain unseen matters, while they are people of uprightness and righteousness — and sometimes they are truthful in that, and sometimes they are wrong.

the answer to this is that they are obliged not to report what they have been made aware of in that regard, and it is forbidden (ḥarām) for them to report it. and if they report some of it and it proves true, the people of faith must not be deceived by it, and must know that this happens to the righteous and to the corrupt, and happens to

t: Obsessive Misgivings Concerning Creed
a: الوساوس في العقيدة
b:
question: a woman whom god has tried with obsessive misgivings and doubts for a long time, and this sometimes brings her to doubt some particulars of creed (ʿaqīdah). what is the remedy for this condition of hers?

answer: this condition is from the work of satan. when she finds anything of that, she should say, "i believe in god", and should increase in the remembrance of god and in seeking forgiveness; for satan quickly withdraws when god, glorified and exalted, is remembered. so if satan whispers to a person in the matter of creed, let him hasten to seek forgiveness and to remember god, be he exalted, and let him increase in remembrance as he is able — for that drives satan away from him and holds him off.

it is soundly established in ṣaḥīḥ muslim, from the hadith of uthman ibn abi al-as al-thaqafi (may god be pleased with him), who said: i came to the messenger of god (may god bless him and grant him peace) and said, "o messenger of god, satan has nearly turned me away from my prayer and my recitation." he said: "that is a devil called khinzab. when you find that, spit dryly to your left three times and say: i seek refuge with god from khinzab."

so the believer must always seek refuge with god from satan, and must know that obsessive misgiving is from his work, and that god, glorified and exalted, forbids him to follow the footsteps of satan — and this is part of following them. so he must not hand the reins to satan; rather let him dissociate himself from him before god and increase in seeking forgiveness, and that obsessive misgiving will quickly depart from him.

then he must also connect himself with the people of faith and the people of strength in god, for satan has no power over them. whoever sits with the people of faith and of strength in god, glorified and exalted, and with the people of the qur’an — satan has no power over him in any circumstance, and flees from him. likewise, one who always prays the five obligatory prayers in the mosque will not, in most cases, be among the people of obsessive misgiving; and likewise one who maintains ritual purity and shields himself from urine will not, in most cases, be among the people of obsessive misgiving. so these matters are a repelling of, and a protection from, obsessive misgiving.

t: The Divisions of the Oneness of God
a: تقسيمات التوحيد
b:
question: we used to hold that the oneness of god (tawḥīd) falls into three categories: what is necessarily true of god, what is impossible of god, be he exalted, and what is possible of him, be he exalted — and likewise concerning the messengers (upon them be blessings and peace). but you said that tawḥīd falls into three categories: belief in [god’s] divinity (ulūhiyyah), belief in [his] lordship (rubūbiyyah), and the oneness of the names and attributes. i would like the two reconciled.

answer: there is no quarrelling over terminology. the division we mentioned is the rational outcome; the division the questioner mentioned only sets out the ranks of the attributes. the attributes, in respect of their being predicated of god, mighty and majestic, fall into these three categories: what a person must believe god to be described by, which is what he has informed [us] about himself; what is possible in that regard, which is the voluntary acts such as providing sustenance, causing death, giving life and so forth; and what is impossible, which is deficiency and defect — this is impossible. as for knowing that in detail — such as enumerating the attributes and confining them to a fixed number, or enumerating the impossible and confining it to a fixed number, or enumerating the possible and confining it to a fixed number — there is no evidence for that.

t: Fatwas on the Hajj and the Lesser Pilgrimage
a: فتاوي في الحج والعمرة
b:
question: is a person sinful who delays the hajj while able to afford it, without excuse?

answer: the hajj is one of the pillars of islam. god, be he exalted, said: {and pilgrimage to the house is a duty owed to god by those people who are able to find a way there; and whoever disbelieves — then god is free of need of the worlds (97)} [āl ʿimrān]. the commander of the faithful, umar ibn al-khattab (may god be pleased with him), said: "i have resolved to send men to these great cities to look at who among them was able to perform the hajj and did not perform it, and to impose the jizyah upon them — they are not muslims, they are not muslims, they are not muslims." and ali (may god be pleased with him) said from the pulpit: "whoever was able to perform the hajj and did not perform it, let him not mind whether he dies a jew or a christian" — for god, be he exalted, said: {and whoever disbelieves — then god is free of need of the worlds (97)} [āl ʿimrān].

on this basis, whoever is able to perform the hajj is obliged to hasten to it. the preponderant view is that the hajj is obligatory immediately (ʿalā al-fawr), not with latitude (ʿalā al-tarākhī), because the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "o people, perform the hajj before you are unable to perform it." they said: "what is the matter with the hajj, o messenger of god?" he said: "its bedouin will sit at the tails of its valleys, and no one will reach the house." and abu dawud transmitted in the sunan, with a chain in which there is weakness, that the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "whoever intends the hajj, let him hasten, for the sick may fall ill, a need may arise, and the mount may stray." these are excuses that prevent the hajj; and therefore a person must hasten to it.

some of the people of knowledge held that the hajj is obligatory with latitude, not immediately, and adduced as evidence that god imposed the hajj upon the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) at the end of the eighth year of the hijrah; then the ninth year came and the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) did not perform the hajj in it, but sent abu bakr to lead the people in the hajj; then in the tenth year the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) performed the farewell pilgrimage. on this basis, the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), after god granted him the conquest of mecca and he was able to perform the hajj in the ninth year, did not perform it in that year but deferred it to another year.

but the answer to this is that the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) would not perform the hajj except in the time of the hajj, and the ninth year was a year of intercalation (nasīʾah). intercalation was practised by the people of the pre-islamic age, and it is the deferral of some of the months from their proper times. the people of mecca made the month of dhu al-hijjah of that year muharram — that is, the month which comes after dhu al-hijjah. they used to do this in the pre-islamic age, and god, be he exalted, abolished it in sūrat al-tawbah, saying therein: {intercalation is only an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray; they make it lawful one year and forbidden another, in order to conform to the number that god has made sacred, and so make lawful what god has forbidden. the evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them} [verse 37]. that is why one of them says: *and we are the ones who intercalate upon maʿadd the months of the profane season, making them sacred.*

and the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said at the farewell pilgrimage: "time has come round as it was on the day god created the heavens and the earth." so he abolished intercalation, and time came round as it was on the day god created the heavens and the earth. god, be he exalted, said: {indeed the number of months with god is twelve months in the book of god, from the day he created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred} [al-tawbah 36]. so time came round as it was on the day god created the heavens and the earth, and the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) performed the hajj at the time of the hajj.

therefore a person able to perform the hajj is considered sinful if he delays it, when he is able and has the capacity. the capacity (istiṭāʿah) which god made a condition in his words {those who are able to find a way there} [āl ʿimrān 97], and which the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) made a condition in the hadith of gabriel in his words "and pilgrimage to the house for whoever is able to find a way there" — its definition is: provision, a mount, and a passable road. "provision" means the expenses; "a mount" means what conveys a person to those places; and "a passable road" means safety for one’s person and property. so if a person finds what will convey him — money for expenses and for transport — and is safe as to his person and his property on the road, then the hajj has become obligatory upon him, and it is not permissible for him to delay its performance. this is the preponderant view, and the evidence supports it.

t: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Tape Four
a: شرح الجزرية الشريط الرابع
b:
then he said: "chapter on the qualities." he set up this chapter for the qualities of the letters. a quality (ṣifah), in origin, is a descriptive attribute, and whatever distinguishes a thing from something else. qualities are, in origin, of three kinds: essential qualities, accidental qualities, and juridically assigned qualities.

the essential qualities are those upon which god created the thing — such as a person's tallness or shortness, his beauty or ugliness, his whiteness or blackness, and the like; this is an essential quality in him.

the accidental qualities are such as the volitional or active qualities — like motion and rest in a person, and speech and silence; this is an accidental quality, that is, one that comes upon the person.

the third kind is the juridically assigned qualities, and they are the rulings that the lawgiver has attached to the thing — such as ritual purity (ṭahārah) and substantive impurity (najāsah). that this thing is pure, and that it is impure, is not part of how it was created, nor is it something accidental in it; rather it is a ruling that the lawgiver has ordered upon it. this is so in the view of the majority of the people of knowledge, as against the hanafis: for the hanafis hold that the juridically assigned qualities are among the original qualities and not among the accidental ones. so they make the rulings foundational, holding that the lawgiver is disclosing what was already there in the original constitution of the thing; and thus they hold that the original state of water is purity, so that this is an original quality of it, and that the original state of urine is impurity, so that this is an original quality of it,

t: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Tape Six

he said that tajwid, in technical usage, is the giving to the letters of their due; and the due of the letters is their necessary qualities, their original qualities, which are these eighteen qualities — this is the letters' due. and "what they merit", in technical usage, is the accidental qualities: the accidental qualities, some of which we have mentioned without covering them exhaustively, such as nasalisation, thinning, thickening and so on. these qualities are called the accidental qualities. so this is a technical usage; otherwise there is no difference in the language between "a due" and "what is merited", because a due is something merited, which the one entitled to it merits. he said:

on the rulings governing the administration of school sponsorship funds

question: there is what is called school sponsorship, provided by a foreign state and administered by a state employee without remuneration. is it open to this administrator to eat from this sponsorship fund, and to take what remains of it after he has administered it as he should — bearing in mind that if he returns it to the body it came from, those persons will use it themselves?

answer: no. he must spend it on the students; and if they have no further need of it and a remainder is left over, let him spend it on the poor of the place where they are. it is not lawful for him to take anything of it for himself.

t: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures at a Packed Event Held by the Youth Association
a: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يحاضر في تظاهرة حاشدة لجمعية الشبيبة
b:
last night, 8 december 2010, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew delivered a lecture entitled "the mission of calling to islam belonging to youth associations", which was organised by the shabibat bina' al-watan association at the square of the cultural and environmental diversity space in nouakchott. the event was packed with great throngs of the association's members and regular attenders, who pressed forward to receive the sheikh and to greet him.

in the lecture his eminence concentrated on the necessity that the idea be sound and be founded on aims and means that accord with the sharia, as islamic alternatives in the field of recreation, criticising those who suppose recreation to be contrary to islam. he said: "associations ought to be founded on a rightly guided basis, so that they may contribute to the service of the muslim homelands… and the collective effort that associations and clubs offer in muslim countries is called for by the sharia, because what is the work of all can only be carried through by the work of all."

the sheikh also concentrated on the importance of calling young people to islam, of whom he said that they are exposed to harshness and extremism, just as they are exposed to moral dissolution and to falling short in religion.

the sheikh surveyed this through examples from the life of the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) with his companions — as when he (peace and blessings be upon him) passed a night with his companions (may god be pleased with them) listening to the chanter, to whom the prophet (may god bless him and grant him peace) said, "gently with the glass vessels", meaning the hearts of the women.

the sheikh strengthened his treatment of the subject with further citations from the life of the companions with the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).

his eminence also urged the necessity of gathering the efforts of these small associations into a single large association, so that it may be of greater worth and more productive.

speaking at the same event was sheikh abd al-rahman ould fatta, who spoke ably of the role of young people and of character, and of the call to bear the trust and to adorn oneself with praiseworthy character.

the moving address was that of the senator umar al-fath, who called on the islamic associations to attend to the aesthetic dimension of their discourse towards the public, each according to his own taste and interests.

t: Answers on the Prophetic Biography
a: أجوبة في السيرة النبوية
b:
from the life of jesus (peace be upon him)

question: did jesus (peace be upon him) wage war, such that he had need to call for helpers (anṣār) in the cause of his mission?

answer: that war is not meant here as confrontation by arms; rather, war comes by every means known to belong to it.

*war is nothing but what you have known and tasted, and it is no matter of conjectural talk.*

war comes through speech, through propaganda and through conspiracies. jesus (peace be upon him) was subjected to many such conspiracies, and was several times subjected to attempts at killing and crucifixion; he was also subjected to many wars of words. so too were the prophets who were his contemporaries: among them zechariah, who was killed in the path of god, and likewise his maternal aunt's son john, who was killed in the path of god; and of the disciples who supported jesus, many were killed in the path of god. as for jesus, god most high raised him to himself: the jews attempted to kill him and to crucify him, and god most high made a likeness of him appear to them, so that they supposed they had killed him and crucified him, whereas in reality they neither killed him nor crucified him — but it was made to appear so to them.

a biographical notice on ibn taymiyyah

question: who is ibn taymiyyah, and is he the shaykh of najd?

answer: that ibn taymiyyah was a man among the muslims, of the people of syria (al-sham), not of the people of najd. he was born in syria in the seventh hijri century and lived there, and he studied and became known among his peers for the excellence of his natural gift and for his intelligence in his boyhood, until he became famous for it, so that when the hadith scholars came to damascus they would come to him and write out for him a tablet of hadith containing sixteen hadiths, and he would memorise it at a single glance. he became known for that in his boyhood, so that one of the great hadith scholars counselled his father not to occupy him with worldly affairs but to devote him to knowledge, in the hope that god might benefit the community (ummah) of muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) through him. his father said to him: "i shall take charge of your worldly affairs on your behalf, so occupy yourself with the affairs of religion," and he set him apart for learning. so he studied in damascus and elsewhere, and travelled through many of god's lands, and he learned until he had memorised close to a million hadiths from the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him). he recited the qur'an according to the ten canonical readings (qirāʾāt), and learned jurisprudence according to the school of the hanbalis, then learned the jurisprudence of the other schools. he was one of the scholars of this community — who are not infallible, who err and who are right. he had errors, as other scholars do, and what he got right was more than what he got wrong. his student ibn al-qayyim (may god have mercy on him) said: the slips of the scholars are filth, and the scholars are seas, and water, when it reaches the two-qullah measure (qullatayn), does not carry impurity.

answer: that he is habib ibn zayd, and that his mother is nasibah (may god be pleased with her). he is the one whom the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) sent to musaylimah. whenever musaylimah asked him, "do you bear witness that there is no god but god and that muhammad is the messenger of god?" he would say, "yes." and when he said, "do you bear witness that i am the messenger of god?" he said, "i am deaf, i do not hear."

the caliphate of abu bakr al-siddiq

question: what are the kinds of succession (khilāfah) that abu bakr al-siddiq assumed?

answer: i do not understand this question. if what is meant is his succeeding the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him), then he assumed the succession to the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in the general office, which is the supreme leadership of this community — namely, establishing the religion and governing worldly affairs by it — and likewise leading the people in prayer, addressing them at the friday prayer, judging between them, commanding their armies and the like. these are the offices of the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him).

abu bakr's assumption of the caliphate.

question: when did abu bakr al-siddiq assume the caliphate?

answer: that he assumed it at the death of the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him). the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him) died in the forenoon of monday and was buried in the forenoon of wednesday

t: Reverent Fear of God
a: الخشية من الله
b:
in the name of god, the most merciful, the most compassionate. praise be to god, lord of the worlds, and i invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his companions and whoever is guided by his guidance and follows his practice until the day of judgement. peace be upon you, and the mercy of god and his blessings. to proceed: reverent fear of god (khashyah), glorified and exalted, is an inducement to complying with his commands, avoiding his prohibitions, dealing well with him and observing propriety with him; and it is likewise an inducement to wariness of his displeasure and his detestation, and to avoiding everything that leads to his displeasure. this reverent fear is one of the stations of the people of faith and one of the levels of the god-conscious, which every person should be eager to reach and, once he has attained it, to hold fast to. god, glorified and exalted, has made clear that reverent fear is a cause of entering the garden, for he said, exalted is he: {indeed those who disbelieve among the people of the book and the idolaters will be in the fire of hell, abiding therein; those are the worst of creatures. indeed those who believe and do righteous deeds — those are the best of creatures. their recompense with their lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. god is pleased with them and they are pleased with him. that is for whoever fears his lord} (sūrat al-bayyinah 98:6–8).

so whoever fears his lord, god has guaranteed him gardens beneath which rivers flow. and god, glorified and exalted, has made clear that reverent fear in its complete sense belongs exclusively to one who knows god most high, for god most high said: {it is only those of his servants who have knowledge that fear god} (sūrat fāṭir 35:28). what is meant by this is true reverent fear. it is not meant by it that everyone who is among the people of reverent fear is among the scholars, nor is it meant by it that everyone who is among the scholars is among the people of reverent fear. rather, what is meant is that true reverent fear comes about only to one who is knowing and recognising of god, glorified and exalted. hence al-ghazali (may god have mercy on him) said: god is disobeyed only out of ignorance of him or of his law. for the ignorance may be of god, glorified and exalted, so that a person is deluded about god and grows bold in disobeying him; and the ignorance may be of god's law, which then entails that a person performs an act while regarding it as permissible (mubāḥ) or as authorised — or perhaps he regards it as an act of worship and a means of nearness to god — while that act is contrary to the law, on account of the person's ignorance of the law.

reverent fear is of varying degrees. among them is that which comes between a person and disobedience, and this measure is the middle degree of reverent fear, and it is what is required of all believers. every person ought to ask god for that measure of reverent fear of him which will come between him and disobedience of him. the measure which entails an awareness of god's watching, glorified and exalted, and fear of his punishment, and that a person should hold present in his mind his majesty, his greatness and his grandeur, and should likewise hold present in his mind his punishment, so that he does not feel secure from his devising — this measure is the constructive measure of reverent fear. if reverent fear increases beyond that, it entails a person's total preoccupation, such that he cannot manage anything and lives permanently in weeping and grief, with an effect upon the mind. this station of reverent fear is not constructive, nor is it required of every person; and if it comes over a person at certain times, that is an added good, but he ought not to remain in it permanently. the lowest station of reverent fear is that a person believes in god, in his power over his creation and in his greatness, but without that having an effect upon him by cutting him off from disobeying him and by avoiding what he has forbidden. this station is not sufficient: reverent fear must increase until it comes between a person and disobedience.

reverent fear has many causes. the most important and greatest of its causes is knowledge of god, majestic is his majesty. for whoever knows god by his grandeur, his greatness, his majesty and his power over his creation, and knows that he is the swiftest of reckoners, and that he is swift in reckoning, and that he is the one who holds the sky from falling upon the earth except by his leave, and that {it is he who holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and were they to cease, no one could hold them after him} (sūrat fāṭir 35:41), and that the seven heavens and the seven earths are in the grasp of his right hand: {they have not esteemed god as he deserves to be esteemed, while the whole earth will be his handful on the day of resurrection and the heavens will be rolled up in his right hand. glorified is he and exalted above what they associate with him} (sūrat al-zumar 39:67); and knows him in that the hearts of all the servants are between two of his fingers, turning them as he wills; and knows him by his nearness, for he is nearer to a person than his jugular vein, and he knows the secret and what is more hidden, so that no thought crosses a person's heart and he thinks no thought whatsoever but it is known to god, glorified and exalted, with a knowledge prior to it, alongside it and after it, so that that knowledge encompasses it from all its sides; and likewise knows him by his favour upon him and his kindness towards him; and knows him likewise by the servant's utter need of him, majestic is his majesty: {o people, you are the ones in need of god, and god is the self-sufficient, the praiseworthy. if he wills, he can do away with you and bring a new creation; and that is not difficult for god} (sūrat fāṭir 35

t: The Means of Uprightness and Steadfastness in Religion
a: وسائل الاستقامة والثبات على الدين
b:
praise belongs to god. we praise him and we seek his help, and we seek refuge in god from the evils of our own selves and from the evil consequences of our deeds. whomever god guides, there is none to lead him astray; and whomever he leads astray, there is none to guide him. i bear witness that there is no god but god alone, having no partner, and i bear witness that muhammad is his servant and his messenger — god bless him and his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace.

{o people, be conscious of your lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate, and from the two of them spread abroad many men and women. and be conscious of god, by whom you ask of one another, and of the ties of kinship. god is ever watchful over you} (sūrat al-nisāʾ 4:1).

{o you who believe, be conscious of god and speak a word that is straight (70). he will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. and whoever obeys god and his messenger has won a great victory} (sūrat al-aḥzāb 33:70–71).

to proceed: the best of speech is the book of god, and the best guidance is the guidance of muhammad, god bless him and grant him peace. the worst of matters are those newly invented in religion, and every innovation in religion (bidʿah) is misguidance.

servants of god, god, glorified and exalted, guides whomever he wills to his straight path, and makes firm upon that path whomever he wills to make firm, and tests people and tries them upon it. whoever god wills to make firm will be made firm.

god, glorified and exalted, has commanded the taking of means in all matters, and among those are the means of guidance and of uprightness. among the means of guidance is learning what god has commanded, and acting upon what the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, brought, and taking the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, as one's model in words, deeds, beliefs and intentions. among the means of guidance likewise is humble entreaty to god, glorified and exalted, in asking for guidance. and among the means of guidance is reflection and remembrance.

then, after that, come the means of steadfastness in the religion of god, and these are greater, and more deserving that the muslim should occupy himself with them.

among the greatest of them is that the muslim should remember that he is in this life within the pattern of mutual pushing back, and within a struggle in which a decisive outcome is unavoidable. this struggle is either uprightness upon the path of guidance until death, or turning back and reversing upon one's heels. people are of two divisions: either a person is of the god-conscious, or he is of the wretched. the god-conscious are the felicitous, whom god makes firm with the firm word in the life of this world and in the hereafter. if a person knows this struggle, and knows the division of people into the two divisions, and knows that this comes about neither by lineage nor by ancestry but only by the taking of means and by the choice of the sovereign, the judge, glorified and exalted, then he will be eager not to be of the wretched, and to be of the people of guidance, and to hold to that his whole life long.

then, among the means of uprightness and steadfastness likewise, is that a person should know the length of this road and what lies upon it of hardships. for many people turn back at the first blow and retreat from the road of uprightness and guidance, and do not stand fast upon it and are not steadfast, because they are ignorant of what lies upon it of blows and obstacles.

you, servants of god, are upon a this-worldly path which is a representation of the path of the hereafter. you know that the path of the hereafter has upon it hooks like the thorns of the saʿdān plant, and that people differ upon it according to their deeds. so likewise this this-worldly path, the white clear way, has upon it hooks that catch hold of people; whoever is not steadfast upon it will turn away upon his heels. god, exalted be he, said: {and among people is he who worships god upon an edge. if good befalls him he is at ease with it, and if a trial befalls him he turns about upon his face. he has lost this world and the hereafter. that is the manifest loss} (sūrat al-ḥajj 22:11).

likewise, among the means of steadfastness in this religion is not to be hasty in a person's attaining his reward in this life. the reward of god, glorified and exalted, is what he has prepared for his friends in the abode of lasting bliss. that reward is god's bringing his friends near, mighty and majestic is he, and his choosing them — when god whitens their faces, gives them their books in their right hands, places them in the first company, brings them near in the highest firdaws of the garden, and shades them with the shade of his throne on a day when there is no shade but his shade; for he has chosen them for that.

therefore a person must be eager for the reward of the hereafter, and must know that what is hastened to him in this life is only a diminishing of his reward. it is established as sound (ṣaḥīḥ) from the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "no raiding party goes out in the path of god and takes spoils but that two thirds of its reward has been hastened to it; and no raiding party goes out in the path of god and fails but that it attains its reward in full."

therefore we must be eager, servants of god, that the hereafter be the bulk of our concern, and that we be eager for the reward of the hereafter, and that we not be eager to hasten anything of our reward in this life.

then know — may god have mercy on me and on you — that those to whom something is hastened in this life, even if they are among the best of the friends of god, always remain in wariness and fear. for that reason al-bukhari and muslim reported in the two ṣaḥīḥ collections from abd al-rahman ibn awf, may god be pleased with him, that he was fasting, and the table was set before him,

t: Good Character
a: حسن الخلق
b:
in the name of god, the merciful, the compassionate. praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds. i pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his companions and whoever is guided by his guidance and takes his sunnah as his way until the day of judgement. peace be upon you, and the mercy of god and his blessings.

to proceed: god, glorified and exalted, made the human being composed of three elements. the first is the intellect, by which he is honoured above the rest of the animals; the second is the body, which is from dust; and the third is the spirit, which is an unseen breath from the command of god. each one of these three elements is capable of cultivation, of growth and of purification. as for the spirit, its growth and its purification come about only through its acquiring praiseworthy character traits and keeping clear of evil ones. a person's good character is evidence of the refinement of his spirit and the purity of his nature, and his bad character is evidence of the foulness of his inward disposition and of the foulness of his spirit — we ask god for safety and well-being.

character is of two kinds: innate character and acquired character. among the character traits there is that which is innate, which a person is created disposed towards and grows accustomed to, as the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "the people of yemen are coming to you. they are the purest of heart and the most tender of heart. faith is yemeni and wisdom is yemeni." the acquired kind is that which a person accustoms himself to, struggling against his own soul until the trait is attained by him.

good character is required by the sharia and is among the highest priorities. for that reason god praised his messenger, god bless him and grant him peace, for good character, saying: {and you are indeed of a magnificent character} (sūrat al-qalam 68:4). so whoever is of good character must necessarily be granted success in the loftiest acts of obedience, and likewise is chosen for the neighbourhood of the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, in the loftiest degrees of the garden. and whoever is of bad character — we ask god for safety and well-being — is not granted success in the greatest acts of obedience, nor is he able to be among the true worshippers, because his bad character entails aversion towards him and his being driven away from the presence and from the elevated station.

a person's acquisition of good character is accomplished only through his knowing the character traits of the believers, and what stands opposite them among the character traits of the unbelievers and the hypocrites, so that he strives to be characterised by the traits of the believers. the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, made that clear: he set out those character traits which, when combined, constitute hypocrisy, so that when they combine in a person he is a pure hypocrite. that is in the report (ḥadīth) of abd allah ibn amr ibn al-as, may god be pleased with them both, that the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "four traits, whoever has them in him is a pure hypocrite; and whoever has one trait of them in him has in him a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, when he makes a covenant he acts treacherously, and when he disputes he behaves outrageously."

the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, likewise set out the marks of the hypocrite, saying: "the sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

standing opposite these are the traits of the people of faith (īmān). among them is truthfulness, for it is one of the traits of faith, in view of what is established from the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to the garden. a man continues to be truthful and to seek out truthfulness until he is written down with god as one who is truthful. and lying guides to wickedness, and wickedness guides to the fire. a man continues to lie and to seek out lying until he is written down with god as a liar."

the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, likewise made clear that the character of this religion is modesty (ḥayāʾ), saying: "every religion has a character, and the character of islam is modesty." and he said of the man of the ansar whom he heard admonishing his brother concerning modesty: "leave him, for modesty is part of faith." it is likewise established from him, god bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "modesty is a branch among the branches of faith."

the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, urged many lofty character traits, such as forbearance and deliberateness, making clear that these two are beloved to god, glorified be his majesty. he said to al-ashajj of abd al-qays: "in you are two traits that god and his messenger love: forbearance and deliberateness."

he likewise made clear that the believer does not lie — that is, he is not a liar by his nature. when he was asked, "does the believer steal?" he said, "yes." it was said, "does the believer commit fornication?" he said, "yes." it was said, "does the believer lie?" he said, "no." what is intended by that is that he is not a liar, one who lies much; for that is not among the traits of the believers, but rather among the traits of the hypocrites.

*his open-handedness of manner entices one to the doing of noble deeds, and respect for him guards you from committing what is base.*

likewise, among the benefits of good character is that it also brings about good companionship and its continuance. relationships are something a person can build, but they are often severed because of a divergence of interests, or because of bad character, or something other than that. so if a person is of good character, the relations

t: The Pillars of Islam, Part One
a: أركان الإسلام الجزء الأول
b:
in the name of god, the most merciful, the ever-merciful.

... and i ask god to bless and grant peace to the one who was sent as a mercy to all the worlds, and to his family, his companions, and all who follow his guidance and keep to his sunnah until the day of judgement. peace be upon you, and the mercy of god and his blessings.

to proceed: god, mighty and majestic, named this religion — the religion with which he sent the noble messenger, may god bless him and grant him peace, to all people — the religion of islam. with it he sealed the religions that came before, and he made it the true religion in the sight of god, glorified and exalted. so every religion other than it, after its coming down and after the sending of muhammad, may god bless him and grant him peace, with it, is thrown back upon those who hold to it: god accepts nothing of it. god, mighty and majestic, was content for his creation with no religion but this one, and he made the earlier religions nothing but a preparation for it,

t: The Pillars of Faith
a: أركان الإيمان
b:
in the name of god, the most merciful, the ever-merciful. all praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds, and i ask god to bless and grant peace to the one who was sent as a mercy to all the worlds, and to his family, his companions, and all who follow his guidance and keep to his sunnah until the day of judgement. peace be upon you, and the mercy of god and his blessings.

to proceed: our subject today is faith (īmān), which god, exalted is he, laid down as a condition (sharţ) upon his servants and for the sake of which he sent the messengers. he said, exalted is he: {they were commanded only to worship god, devoting their religion to him sincerely, as people of pure faith, and to establish the prayer and to give zakat — that is the religion of the upright community (5)} [sūrat al-bayyinah 98:5]. for its sake god, mighty and majestic, is known, and his books and his messengers are known. for its sake a person believes in god's decree (qaḍāʾ) and in his determination, which takes effect. and for its sake a person believes in the last day and in the raising up after death.

t: The Signs of the Hour, Part One
a: أشراط الساعة الجزء الأول
b:
in the name of god, the most merciful, the ever-merciful. all praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds, and i ask god to bless and grant peace to the one who was sent as a mercy to all the worlds, and to his family, his companions, and all who follow his guidance and keep to his sunnah until the day of judgement.

to proceed: god, glorified and exalted, has told us that the hour is coming, in which there is no doubt, and he has made clear that this community (ummah) is the last of the communities. it is the seal of the communities, and the hour will not come except upon those left of it. the hour is a momentous event, and it requires of this community that it make itself ready to be the close of this world, and that it prepare itself to be the opening of the next. for we are the last to come, the foremost, as the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, said. with this community this world is sealed, so it is the world's last community; and with it the hour is opened, so it is the hour's first community. the first of the communities to be summoned before god is this community,

t: The Signs of the Hour, Part Two
a: أشراط الساعة الجزء الثاني
b:
whoever does not believe until after he has seen the major signs — his faith will avail him nothing with god, because it is like the faith of a drowning man after he has already drowned, as was the case with pharaoh when he said: {i believe that there is no god but the one in whom the children of israel believe, and i am one of those who submit.} (sūrat yūnus 10:90).

as for the minor signs, the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, set out some of them in gabriel's questioning, when he asked him and said: 'then tell me about its marks.' he said: 'that the bondwoman will give birth to her mistress' — and in another narration, 'to her master' — 'and that you will see the barefoot, the naked, the destitute herdsmen of sheep competing with one another in raising tall buildings.' so here the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, set out, among the minor signs of the hour, that the bondwoman will give birth to her mistress — and in another narration, that the bondwoman will give birth to her master,
