(an encyclopaedia) that has gathered hadith with its sources traced, that has gathered the book recited in measure and expounded; that has gathered the prophet's traits (shamāʾil), the campaigns (maghāzī), the raiding parties (sarāyā) and the expeditions, and all that took place in them. so he fancies that he has lived among his companions an age, hearing the hadith in it and seeing. and he fancies the horses of god before him, their squadrons standing firm, raising the dust. and he says: what are the films, the relics and the stirring tales, when they are seen, but hurried glimpses that handle one single element — and most of them a fabricated report. but that which al-sharif has been guided to gather and to order, or what has come forth from him of it, is a truthful exposition of all the elements, one that makes the truth plain and leaves no element out. how excellent is our sharif and his comrades! how truthful are these folk — indeed, how patient! they have made new what they laid down, and brought that beside which those who prize it would count a jewel cheap. o lord, grant victory to (nasir) and honour him, and open for him, o lord, a greater opening; and guard him from the evils of the envious, and turn them back in surrender, retreating, when they see him. and continue your blessing and your peace upon him whom you have ennobled and raised to the highest summits.*

t: Qatar Television Hosts the Sheikh on the Programme "Life of the Hearts"
a: تلفزيون قطر يستضيف الشيخ في برنامج حياة القلوب
b: qatar television hosted his eminence the erudite sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew yesterday, friday, on the programme "life of the hearts" at ten in the morning, on the subject: "the constituents of the contemporary islamic personality". the sheikh spoke on the subject "the constituents of the contemporary islamic personality", on the concept of constituents and on the human being's need to develop the three natural capacities: spirit, body and intellect. he explained that islam has set out for each kind of these capacities a mode of address that goes along and accords with the innate human disposition (fiṭrah) and that secures for him every benefit and every desire that profits him in this world and the next. his eminence also stressed that the constituents of the muslim personality are attained only by building four necessary stages: 1 — seeking knowledge; 2 — acting upon what one has learned; 3 — calling people to islam (daʿwah); 4 — patience upon the path of truth. these four constituents are the embodiment of the words of god most high in sūrat al-ʿaṣr: {by time. truly man is in loss, save those who believe and do righteous deeds, and enjoin one another to truth, and enjoin one another to patience.} (sūrat al-ʿaṣr 103:1–3). his eminence mentioned that the exemplary muslim personality is the one god — glorified and exalted is he — has made a model for humankind and commanded us to follow, and that it is embodied in the person of the prophet — may god bless him and grant him peace — in bearing and in method.

t: The Causes of the Punishment of the Grave
a: أسباب عذاب القبر
b:
what is the best deed for deliverance from the punishment of the grave?

the punishment of the grave has causes that lead to it. among them is failing to shield oneself from urine and failing to keep clean of it; among them is going about with talebearing (namīmah); among them is lying; and other things besides, such as leaving off the payment of zakat. these sins are a cause of the punishment of the grave. so if a person avoids these sins, god — glorified and exalted is he — will deliver him, if he wills, from the punishment of the grave.

t: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, Head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, Takes Part in the Conference on the Prophetic Sunnah
a: الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء يشارك في مؤتمر السنة النبوية
b:
sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, head of the centre for the formation of scholars, took part in the fourth colloquium held in the wilaya of constantine in algeria, under the title: "the prophetic sunnah in the face of doubts and challenges. the colloquium opened on monday 11 april 2011, and sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, head of the centre for the formation of scholars, delivered the address of the delegations at the colloquium's opening session and chaired the first of its sessions.

in the programme accompanying the colloquium, the sheikh — may god preserve him — gave a lecture on the evening of the same day at the emir abd al-qadir mosque in constantine, after the sunset prayer, and gave a lesson of guidance for the imams after the night prayer at the premises of the house of the imam. the association of algerian muslim scholars in constantine had organised a ceremony in the sheikh's honour on the evening of that same monday. on the second day of the colloquium, his eminence sheikh al-dedew delivered an address in the second session of the evening period, under the title: "the sunnah in the view of the modernists". the site will, god willing, publish the sheikh's contributions to this colloquium later.

t: His Eminence the Sheikh Takes Part in the First World Conference of Researchers in the Noble Qur'an and its Sciences
a: فضيلة الشيخ يشارك فى المؤتمر العالمي الأول للباحثين فى القرءان الكريم وعلومه .
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew took part — in his capacity as head of the centre for the formation of scholars, as an adviser in the world authority for inimitability, and as deputy for the president of the international union of muslim scholars — in the first world conference of researchers in the noble qur'an and its sciences, which the moroccan city of fez hosted in the period 10–12 jumada al-ula 1432 ah, corresponding to 14–16 april 2011 ce. the conference was organised this year under the banner: "the efforts of the community in the service of the noble qur'an and its sciences".

at the conference's opening ceremony his eminence the sheikh delivered an address in the name of the president of the international union of muslim scholars, his eminence sheikh yusuf al-qaradawi, in which he said that god, mighty and majestic, honoured the community with this mighty book, which its various generations have served, from the companions — may god be pleased with them — down to the scholars of the community across the ages. his eminence said that in this age the means have become abundantly available, whereas the community's forebears among the great scholars used to expend exhausting efforts in the service of god's mighty book. the sheikh also made valuable contributions in the conference's various events.

we in the site's administration will furnish you with a complete file on the sheikh's contributions to this important conference, at a later time, god most high willing.

t: Questions [1]
a: الأسئلة [1]
b:
## some of the poetry of the jinn, and how far it is soundly established

**the question:** the scholars record poems of the jinn in their books. how were these poems transmitted, and how did they come to know that they were soundly established?

**the answer:** as regards the poems and the utterances reported from the jinn and transmitted in the books of the prophet's biography (sīrah) — many of these old books have authors of whom lying is not to be thought, such as muhammad ibn ishaq, who is very close in time to the events, since he is among the senior successors of the successors. he met a great number of the successors and his period is near, so these reports are transmitted from the companions.

some of their poems have been soundly established among what is transmitted in ṣaḥīḥ al-bukhari, such as their weeping over umar ibn al-khattab, and such as their poems at the time of the emigration — for some of them were muslims whom the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, did not know at that time. among them is the crier whom the people of mecca heard, making known the affair of umm maʿbad:

*may god reward on our behalf — and the reward is of his bounty — two companions who alighted at the two tents of umm maʿbad. they came down with the truth and departed with it; so how fortunate is he who has become the companion of muhammad.* …

t: Questions [2]
a: الأسئلة [2]
b:
## obsessive misgiving is obedience to satan

**the question:** i find obsessive misgiving (waswasah) in the full ritual washing (ghusl), so that i spend thirty or forty-five minutes at it. a great deal of time is wasted, and every time i have washed a limb it seems to me that i have not washed it, so i go back to it — and the same with the hair of the head, or the beard — and a great deal of time is wasted in it.

**the answer:** this person is afflicted with obsessive misgiving, and it is of satan's doing. he must beware of giving satan a way against him. he must not obey satan while knowing that he is his enemy; rather he must obey god, and keep away from satan's doing. and when satan tells him that he has not done a thing, let him rub satan's nose in the dust and abandon what has been cast upon him.

accordingly, whoever feels obsessive misgiving must take often to seeking refuge with god from the accursed satan, truthful in his heart; and he must not follow satan's promptings. so when he has washed a limb, let him pass on from it and wash another; and if satan makes it seem to him that he has not finished, let him not go back over himself in that, nor look at it — because satan may make him see that he has not yet washed …

t: Sheikh al-Dedew, President of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, Lectures in Kuwait on the Role of the Expatriate in Serving the Homeland
a: الشيخ الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء يحاضر في الكويت عن دور المغترب في خدمة الأوطان
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, delivered a lecture in kuwait entitled "the role of emigrant communities in serving their homelands", organised by the league of the mauritanian community in kuwait at the kuwait continental hotel, on 18/05/2011.

in his talk the sheikh addressed the opportunities available to a person in this world, and the necessity of using this short lifespan in beneficial knowledge and in lawful earning.

the sheikh said that god, exalted is he, has decreed migrations in the earth upon the children of man. among these migrations are those undertaken in search of knowledge and of provision, and among them are migrations of flight from straitness and distress and in search of freedom.

the sheikh went on at some length in mentioning patterns and examples of these migrations, taking guidance from the migrations of the prophets, peace be upon them, and from examples among the shinqiti emigrants.

in his lecture the sheikh concentrated on directing the community towards the praiseworthy character an emigrant ought to display, and the effective role he undertakes in serving his homeland materially and morally. he also urged the community to be a good embassy for its homeland in knowledge and in character.

the sheikh warned against the passivity and ossification that afflicts some communities, such that they cut themselves off from the mother country and do not integrate into the new society, and so become unsteady in their belonging and in their representation.

the sheikh called upon those living abroad and upon emigrants to keep their bond with the homeland and to serve it by every available means, and called upon them likewise to develop themselves and to make use of the expertise and the experience that contact with others affords, so as to contribute to reforming their homelands and to raising the awareness of their societies.

poetry and letters had their presence, despite the shortness of the time, as the poets did not let slip the opportunity to welcome the sheikh and to acclaim his standing and his contributions in calling people to islam, in scholarship and in reform.

the lecture [drew] a notable attendance from members of the community, and some guests from among the kuwaiti brethren also attended.

at the end of the lecture a shield of appreciation was presented to the sheikh by the league of the mauritanian community, for the great roles his eminence undertakes in making the country's culture known and in representing it in scholarly gatherings.

the lecture was organised by the league of the mauritanian community in kuwait, as part of scholarly and cultural activities the league holds in order to activate the bridge of communication among the community itself on the one hand, and between them and their homeland on the other.

t: Replies to Questions Sent to the Site, Part 2
a: ردود على الأسئلة الواردة للموقع ج2
b:
**question:** what is the ruling on studying on a scholarship to australia, given that i tried to complete my studies in my own country and was not able to, and my specialisation is computing?

**answer:** praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds. to proceed: the ruling on studying abroad on a scholarship, anywhere in the world, takes on whichever of the rulings applies according to the intention of the one who does it. if the one who does it intends by it to raise the standing of this community and to serve it, and to discharge the communally obligatory duties (furūḍ al-kifāyāt), then he is one striving in the path of god by his study and his scholarship, and he is rewarded for everything that befalls him and for all the time he spends outside his country. the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, sent zayd ibn thabit al-ansari to the jews to learn their language, on a mission of that kind, and that is the basis of the permissibility of studying abroad on a scholarship.

but a person must know the rulings that govern studying abroad, and must prepare for it, for he is exposed to many trials. he must know the rulings on the dispensations (rukhaṣ) in what concerns the prayer and the fast, and he must know also the rulings on mixing with women who are not close relatives (ajnabiyyāt) and on looking at them, for he is exposed to great trials, and so he must be careful in this. in addition, he must also be careful, in the place of his study, that there be near him a mosque or an islamic centre in which he may attend the friday prayer and the congregational prayers together with the muslims. for any city in which there is no mosque for the muslims — residence in it is not lawful except under compulsion.

the compilers of the sunan collections reported that the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, said: "i am quit of every muslim who resides among the idolaters, such that their two fires are not visible to one another." that is where he is alone, with no muslim with him, so that if he were to die there would be one to attend him, to prepare his body and to bury him. but as for one who is in a country in which there are muslims who are able to establish the rites — al-hafiz ibn hajar mentioned in al-fatḥ, from al-mawardi, that a country becomes an abode of islam by the presence of muslims in it.

---

**question:** what is called in hassaniya *aṭlayṣah*: a man who lends money to people. you come to him wanting, say, a million ouguiya. he says to you: i will give you the million for a million three hundred, and you agree to that. he goes with you to the market and buys you goods for the very same million that is in his pocket, and hands the goods over to you, and you sell them to someone else for less than that price; and after a year you give him a million three hundred in cash.

is it permissible for me to take cash in this way??

**answer:** no. this is one of the stratagems used to reach usurious gain (ribā), and the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, forbade them. he said that when god forbids a thing he forbids its price: "god cursed the jews — god forbade them the fats, and they rendered them down and sold them and consumed their price." for this reason a person must beware of usurious gain and of everything that comes near it. the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who consumes usurious gain, the one who pays it, the one who records it and its two witnesses, and said: they are alike.

likewise the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, made plain the prohibition of these stratagems. when a man came to him bringing dates from khaybar — janīb dates, which are the best kind of dates — he said to him: "are all the dates of khaybar like this?" he said: "no; we sell one measure of janīb for two measures of the mixed sort, the jamʿ." he said: "do not do so. that is ribāʾ" — that is, usurious gain — "sell the jamʿ for dirhams, then buy janīb with the dirhams."

and it has come down from him, in the musnad of imam ahmad and the mustadrak of al-hakim, that he said: "one single dirham of usurious gain that a man consumes is graver than thirty-six acts of fornication." god, exalted is he, has forbidden usurious gain and made plain its harm in the hereafter. he said, exalted is he: {those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands whom satan has prostrated by his touch. that is because they said: trade is only like usury. but god has permitted trade and has forbidden usury. so whoever receives an admonition from his lord and desists, he may keep what is past, and his affair rests with god; but whoever returns — those are the companions of the fire, in which they abide for ever. (275) god blights usury and causes acts of charity to grow, and god does not love any ungrateful sinner. (276) indeed those who believe and do righteous deeds and establish the prayer and give the zakat — they have their reward with their lord, and no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve. (277) o you who believe, be mindful of god and give up what remains of usury, if you are believers. (278) and if you do not, then be notified of a war from god and his messenger. but if you repent, you may have your principal sums — you neither wrong nor are wronged. (279)} (sūrat al-baqarah 2:275-279).

so a person must repent of this transaction and must not embark upon it thereafter; and if he has already embarked upon it, let him repent. the repentance of the one who consumes usurious gain differs from the repentance of the one who pays it. the one who pays it is obliged, in his repentance, to do no more than seek forgiveness, and to intend not to return to it, and to resolve upon that, and to feel remorse for what he neglected of his duty towards god. as for the one who consumes usurious gain, he is obliged to return with repentance and remorse, and to give back what he took of usurious gain and so rid himself of it:

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Presides over the Ceremony Closing the 2010–2011 Academic Year at the Centre for the Formation of Scholars
a: الشيخ الددو يترأس حفل اختتام العام الدراسـي 2010-2011 لمركز تكوين العلماء.
b:
during the ceremony closing the 2010–2011 academic year, held by the centre for the formation of scholars at its premises in arafat on the evening of yesterday, thursday 30/06/2011, after the sunset prayer, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew — president of the centre — delivered a formal address in which he welcomed the honoured guests who had answered the invitation. among them were the ambassadors of saudi arabia, kuwait and qatar, and the director of the chinguitel company, as well as the deputy head of the urban community, the assistant governor of nouakchott, the prefect of arafat, businessmen and heads of institutions, besides a large gathering of scholars, judges, notables, imams and preachers.

at the opening of his address sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew affirmed that those running the centre had wanted to combine the two goods, drawing on the strengths of the traditional maḥẓarah and of the modern school while avoiding the weaknesses of both, noting that all the centre's students memorise the qur'an and have a daily programme of memorisation for the noble hadith and for the remaining scholarly primers (mutūn).

the sheikh stated that the centre is open to all muslims and has no nationality, even though it stands on mauritanian soil, thanking the official authorities for making it possible to open the centre to all muslims, and affirming that the centre's guests and students have always been made welcome at the official level.

sheikh al-dedew indicated that the centre for the formation of scholars maintains relations of cooperation and exchange with international centres and with local ones, and that it has seen a large turnout in past years from scholars and students of knowledge. he affirmed that the centre's essential mission lies in its scholarly character: it has nothing to do with politics, nor with sociology, nor with ideological thought. it is a scholarly centre concerned with graduating a company of people of learning with a godly cast, "because knowledge is a weapon that can only be placed in a trustworthy hand" — in sheikh al-dedew's own words.

the ceremony also included an address by the director general of the centre for the formation of scholars, dr muhammad al-mukhtar ould muhammad al-mami, on the centre's aims and its educational systems, in which he indicated that "the centre is nothing but one link in the chain of giving in this giving country; it is an extension of the ancient shinqiti maḥẓarah, whose light illumined these regions and bore the torch of guidance into every quarter of the world.

the centre's director affirmed that those who run it wish through it to preserve that inherited glory, so that grandson after grandson may inherit it, drawing in this on what modern educational methods have arrived at in the way of means and instruments, and adding to it what they regard as necessary of the knowledge of languages, the study of the fundamentals of economics and law, training in computing, and whatever else is necessary for a student of the sharia sciences, so that he may be balanced in personality and complete in vision and able to convey the religion in the idiom of the age — while avoiding, in this centre, certain of the maḥẓarah's practices that were the product of its own environment.

he added that the centre's students number, to date, 102: of these, 12 are at the university stage and 90 at the intermediate and secondary stage. the first cohort at the centre will graduate next year. the centre allocates 10 per cent of its places each year to non-mauritanian students, and the teaching staff number 20.

the centre's director spoke about the imams and preachers project, which comprises 25 imams and preachers, among them 6 women preachers, besides 40 women who are being trained under a special programme that takes account of what is particular to women and of their scholarly and daʿwah needs.

the centre's director said that study proceeds by stages, in three phases: a first, equivalent to secondary level in the original sciences, lasting four years, in which the books and the abridgements (mukhtaṣarāt) are studied; a second, equivalent to university level, lasting four years, in which the extended works are studied; and a third, equivalent to postgraduate study in its two phases of master's and doctorate, whose aim is to deepen the sharia and linguistic disciplines and which concludes with in-depth research. across the three phases the student studies fifty-two disciplines.

among the items of the ceremony was an address on behalf of the teaching staff delivered by sheikh shaykhna ould sid al-hajj, who in his eloquent educational address surveyed the efforts of the scholars in this country and stirred the students' resolve to diligence and perseverance in their studies.

the students and the students' representatives, in their interventions at the ceremony, likewise expressed their pleasure at the scholarly efforts the centre is making, unprecedented in the country's history, and called on everyone to support its efforts so that its noble message may be carried through.

at the close of the ceremony five shields were presented to the institutions supporting the centre, and thirty prizes were distributed to the students who had excelled in the examination and in the poetry and oratory competition. among these prizes was a ticket for the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah) to the holy places, besides substantial cash prizes.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew a Standing Guest on the 4Shbab Channel throughout Ramadan on the Programme "Concepts", Part 3
a: الشيخ الددو ضيف دائم على قناة فور شباب طيلة أيام شهر رمضان في برنامج مفاهيم ج3
b:
the 4shbab channel is hosting his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, on the programme "concepts" (part three), as a standing guest of the programme, throughout the days of the noble month of ramadan. in these episodes the sheikh is in conversation with dr ʿadil banaʿmah.

this programme is broadcast every day of the blessed month at half past five in the evening, mecca time — 1:30 in the afternoon, universal time — and is repeated at half past six in the evening, mecca time — 3:30 in the morning, universal time.

the programme "concepts" (part three) is concerned with the terms and concepts current among young people generally, whether they are concepts of the sharia, or educational, or daʿwah-related, or social ones.

it throws light on them by bringing out their correct meaning and the limits of their acceptable applications, and by pointing to the error that occurs in them at the level of understanding or at the level of application, proceeding in this from the criteria of the sharia and from regard for the jurisprudence of issuing legal opinions and for circumstances, within the moderate, middle-way approach.

we note too that there are other programmes with the sheikh broadcast on other channels during the noble month, among them the dalil channel, the al-risalah channel, and mauritanian national television. their times will be announced at a later date before they are broadcast, and we accordingly draw attention to their importance and invite the honoured public to take advantage of this precious ramadan opportunity.

those running the site will work, god willing, to keep pace with the episodes of this programme, to broadcast them live on the site, and to post them in the section set aside for them among the site's new material, together with a summary of their most important ideas and a simplification of their meanings, so that benefit may be had and may become general.

t: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures at the Research and Studies Centre of the Islamic Development Bank in Jeddah
a: سماحة الشيخ  الددو  يحاضر في مركز البحوث والدراسات بالبنك الإسلامي للتنمية بجدة .
b:
his eminence sheikh al-dedew lectures at the research and studies centre of the islamic development bank in jeddah.

his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, delivered a lecture at the research and studies centre of the islamic development bank in jeddah today, monday (15/09/1432 ah), corresponding to (15/09/2011 ce), under the title: the foundations of transactions (muʿāmalāt) in the islamic sharia. in it he took up:

• the nature of the sharia in setting out rulings, comparing it with man-made law, and showing that the sharia states rulings with their operative causes (ʿilal) and grounds given, whereas the man-made laws state them stripped of that.

• the qur'anic texts that deal with the contract, and the aspects of it that they deal with.

• contracts [that are] prohibited, and the respects in which they are prohibited, in general terms.

• the conditions (shurūṭ) of contracts, in general terms.

• the respects in which contracts are given latitude and the respects in which they are restricted.

the lecture closed with discussions from those present on a number of the questions the lecture had raised.

the lecture was chaired by professor dr al-ʿayyashi faddad, the economic expert, and was attended by a large gathering of researchers at the bank's centre for studies and research and of those concerned with islamic transactions.

his eminence the sheikh was also received privately by his excellency professor dr ahmad muhammad ʿali, director of the islamic development bank, and by his senior aides, in his office before the lecture.

t: His Eminence the Sheikh Lectures at Moulay Ismail University on "The Sharia Sciences and Society"
a: سماحة الشيخ يحاضر في جامعة مولاي إسماعيل حول( العلوم الشرعية والمجتمع )
b:
on the occasion of the opening of the academic year at the faculty of letters of moulay ismail university in meknes, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, delivered a lecture in the faculty's main hall under the title: (the sharia sciences and society). the attendance was notable for its variety, taking in the president of the city's scholarly council, the dean of the faculty, the head of the islamic studies department, and a large number of teaching staff and students.

he also delivered another important lecture under the title: (the community's priorities for carrying out the bearing of witness).

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures in the City of Zouerate at the Invitation of the Future Association for Daʿwah, Culture and Education
a: الشيخ الددو يُحاضر بمدينة ازويرات بدعوة من جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم
b:
his eminence the learned sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, delivered a series of lectures in the city of zouerate on 17 october 2011, at the invitation of the future association for daʿwah, culture and education.

the first lecture was given at the premises of the women's maḥẓarah in zouerate at nine in the morning, under the title "reflections on sūrat al-ḥujurāt".

at five in the evening the sheikh, may god preserve him, gave the second lecture at the premises of the zouerate cinema, entitled "islam is responsibility and character", organised in cooperation between the future association for daʿwah, culture and education and the bina' zemmour association.

his eminence also gave the third and last lecture at the al-ridwan mosque in the city centre after the sunset prayer, entitled "concepts that must be corrected" (the concept of worship; of religiosity; of stewardship on the earth).

this daʿwah activity, called for and organised by the future association for daʿwah, culture and education, was attended by a large crowd of the young people of the city of zouerate, besides a notable attendance of all ages, men and women, from every section of society.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew, President of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, Lectures in Qatar on "Disagreement — a Pattern Established in Creation"
a: الشيخ الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء يُحاضر في موضوع "الاختلاف.. سنة كونية" بدولة قطر
b:
the institute of daʿwah and islamic sciences in doha hosted his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, on the evening of yesterday, monday 05 december 2012, to give a course of instruction at the mosque of ʿumar ibn al-khattab in doha, entitled "the jurisprudence of disagreement — a pattern established in creation (sunnah kawniyyah)".

dr muhammad ibn salah ibrahim, president of the institute of daʿwah and islamic sciences, stated at the opening that "this course is important, in that it takes up an important subject that we all have need of — namely disagreement and what follows from it — especially as it acquaints us with the disagreement of the scholars and how it was, and with their way of dealing with one who differs from them.

this course takes up several strands, turning on:

1. disagreement and its kinds.

2. the kinds of those who differ, and dealing with them.

before the course the sheikh gave three lectures: one of them on sorcery — prevention and treatment; the second on "the evil eye is real" and what has come down on that in the prophetic reports; and the third on: "how to treat yourself by means of the ruqyah sanctioned by the sharia.

the site will publish the lectures of that course later, god willing, together with a summary of them, to bring them within reach of students and of those interested.

t: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Meets the Shaykh of al-Azhar in Cairo
a: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يلتقي في القاهرة بشيخ الأزهر الشريف
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, is making a visit to the republic of egypt, in the course of which he paid today, sunday 16 muharram 1433, corresponding to 11/12/2011, a visit of cooperation and brotherhood to the seat of al-azhar in the egyptian capital, cairo, where his eminence was received by his eminence dr ahmad al-tayyib, shaykh of al-azhar, at the headquarters of the mashyakhah of al-azhar, in the presence of his eminence dr safwat hijazi, secretary general of the league of scholars of the people of the sunnah.

during the meeting his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew spoke about the experience of the centre for the formation of scholars and the scholarly role it undertakes in forming scholars who combine the encyclopaedic breadth of the graduates of the maḥāẓir with the specialisation of those who graduate under contemporary curricula. the sheikh went on, in his name as president of the ʿabd allah ibn yasin university, to speak about that new university, affirming that it works to provide an academic environment covering a number of important and varied specialisms, within an integrated educational system.

his eminence the shaykh of al-azhar welcomed this scholarly activity, aimed at spreading the knowledge of the sharia according to the school of the people of the sunnah and the community, which has continued to distinguish the land of shinqit, situated in the far west of the islamic world. his eminence affirmed al-azhar's readiness for scholarly cooperation with the two institutions — the centre for the formation of scholars and the ʿabd allah ibn yasin university in nouakchott — and with their counterparts in mauritania and in the other countries of the brotherly islamic west.

t: His Eminence the Sheikh Makes Condolence Visits to the Families of Scholars and Notables in the Interior
a: فضيلة الشيخ يقوم بزيارات تعزية لأسر علماء وأعيان في الداخل
b:
on sunday and monday, 23–24 muharram 1433, corresponding to 18–19/12/2011, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew paid the duty of condolence to a number of families in the interior, following the deaths of several eminent scholars and local notables at the end of last week.

his eminence visited in particular the family of ahl al-shaykh sidiya in boutilimit, to offer its members condolences on the death of the late general khalifah of the family of ahl al-shaykh sidiya, his eminence sheikh ʿabd al-rahman ibn muhammad ibn sid al-mukhtar ibn al-shaykh sidiya.

his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew also visited the family of ahl al-shaykh al-qadi in the village of boutalhaya, and offered his condolences on the death of the late general khalifah of ahl al-shaykh al-qadi, his eminence sheikh al-mustafa ibn al-shaykh al-qadi.

his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew made a further visit to the family of ahl abat, to offer its members condolences on the death of the godly scholar, the learned muhammad abat ould muhammad ould ahmad wal abat, sheikh of the maḥẓarah of umm al-nuwar in assaba.

his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew also made a visit to the family of ahl ahmad zaydan in kamour, to offer its members condolences on the death of his eminence sheikh muhammad yahya ould bab ould ahmad zaydan, may god almighty have mercy on him.

during this journey his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew met the notables of the communes of kamour and al-ghayrah, and on the margins of those meetings gave some directions and counsel to the women's gatherings in the two areas, in cooperation with the women's association.

a number of sheikhs accompanied the sheikh on this journey, among them in particular: ʿabd al-rahman al-dakhil; sidi mawlud ould jakir; amadi ould sid al-mukhtar; muhammad al-hasan ould amud; and shaykhna ould sidi al-hajj.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Presides over the Opening of the Islamic Economics Department at Ibn Yasin University
a: الشيخ الددو يشرف على افتتاح قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي بجامعة ابن ياسين
b:
the premises of ʿabd allah ibn yasin university in nouakchott hosted, on the evening of today, tuesday 25 muharram 1433, corresponding to 20/12/2011, an official ceremony for the launch of the university's islamic economics department.

the university's president, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, presided over the opening of the department, in the presence of the university's administrative and academic staff and an audience of its students and of those interested in scholarly affairs. the ceremony was opened by the coordinator of the newly created islamic economics department, dr muhammad ould sid oubek, who welcomed the president, the university's staff and the audience present, recalling the importance of the university's launching this department, which is being opened for the first time in the country and which begins by receiving students holding the baccalaureate and the licence, offering them an academic training which the university has been careful to make conform to the scholarly standards adopted in this field.

the floor then passed to the university's president, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, who drew attention to the university's opening of its new department, which completes the various courses of training studied within the university, and congratulated the administrative staff on smoothing away every difficulty in the way of opening a department concerned with research in a field as vital as islamic economics. in his formal address on behalf of the university the sheikh offered his thanks to the government and the public authorities for their cooperation with the university, expressing the hope that this cooperation would be strengthened so that the university might realise its ambitions for a complete modern academic education, and looking forward to the university's providing, through the islamic economics department, the scholarly consultancy needed by the islamic banks operating in the country — thereby contributing to the resolution of some of the problems raised for those working in the field of islamic banking in the various countries of the world.

in turn the university's vice-president, dr muhammad salim ould al-khu, took the floor, welcoming those present and thanking his eminence the sheikh for the attention he gives to scholarly attainment through his opening of this department today. he also thanked the doctors for the cooperation they have never ceased to give towards realising the mission of ibn yasin university, and for the scholarly and research efforts they make to develop the university's performance and to raise the level of its graduates in its various departments and specialisms.

finally the floor was opened to the audience, and a number of the doctors teaching at the university came forward to the platform, expressing their thanks to the university for opening this department. in their turn the students who spoke affirmed the importance of this department, recording that the university had taken the lead in opening this department concerned with islamic economics.

t: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures in Kuwait on the Effect of the Language Sciences on Understanding the Rulings of the Book and the Sunnah
a: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يحاضر في الكويت عن أثر علوم اللغة في فهم أحكام الكتاب والسنة
b:
yesterday, saturday 29 muharram 1433, corresponding to 24/12/2011, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew delivered a scholarly lecture at the premises of the "mujaddid" centre for the formation of scholars and memorisers of the qur'an in the state of kuwait, under the title: "the effect of the language sciences on understanding the rulings of the book and the sunnah".

in this lecture the sheikh took up in detail the effects of the various language sciences (grammar (naḥw), morphology (ṣarf), pre-islamic poetry, rhetoric (balāghah)…) on the understanding of the rulings of the sharia, and the role of these sciences in grasping the significations of the texts bearing on rulings in the book and the sunnah. through this lecture the sheikh set out for the students of the "mujaddid" centre for the formation of scholars and memorisers of the qur'an a grounding in the necessity of deep mastery of the various sciences connected with the arabic language, as the instrument that assists in grasping the texts of the sharia relied on in deriving rulings according to the facts of cases and to newly arising matters.

this lecture comes within the participation of his eminence sheikh al-dedew, may god preserve him, in the programme organised by the "mujaddid" centre for the formation of scholars and memorisers of the qur'an in kuwait under the banner: "days and nights of our arabic language — the language of religion and of the world", during the visit he is making to the state of kuwait to take part in numerous scholarly events, festivals and conferences.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Delivers Lectures in the Ibn Qudamah Course at the Cultural Centre of the Sheikh Eid Charitable Foundation in Doha
a: الشيخ الددو يُلقي محاضرات في دورة ابن قدامة بالمركز الثقافي لمؤسسة عيد الخيرية بالدوحة
b:
on the evening of yesterday, saturday 19 rabi' al-awwal 1433 ah, corresponding to 11/02/2012, the ibn qudamah course in the sharia sciences began, organised by the cultural centre of the sheikh eid charitable foundation in the state of qatar, in doha. sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, is taking part in this course by giving lessons and lectures at the course's second level, which is held at the al-mani' mosque in the al-waab district of doha. the course runs for eight days.

sheikh al-dedew's programme comprises three lessons a day for the duration of the course. the first lesson begins half an hour after the dawn prayer (fajr) and is on the technical terminology of hadith (muṣṭalaḥ al-ḥadīth); in it the sheikh expounds the book al-bāʿith al-ḥathīth fī sharḥ ikhtiṣār ʿulūm al-ḥadīth of al-hafiz ibn kathir. the second lesson is in legal theory (uṣūl al-fiqh), half an hour after the night prayer (ʿishāʾ); in it he expounds the book al-tamhīd fī takhrīj al-furūʿ ʿalā al-uṣūl of al-isnawi. the third lesson is in the language sciences and literature, after the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr); in it he expounds passages from the seven suspended odes.

the course is meeting a large turnout from the general public and from the specialists among students of knowledge, from inside qatar and outside it. it is an intensive scholarly course in which a number of scholarly primers across the various sharia sciences are taught and in which a select group of specialists takes part. the site will, god willing, keep pace with the sheikh's latest lectures in this course and will upload them in edited form for the benefit of its esteemed visitors.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in the International Forum for Heads of Arabic Departments in African Universities, in Mecca
a: الشيخ الددو يشارك في الملتقى الدولي لرؤساء أقسام العربية في الجامعات الإفريقية بمكة
b:
sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of abdullah ibn yasin university, is taking part in the proceedings of an international scholarly forum hosted by mecca the ennobled, in his capacity as the representative of ibn yasin university; the conference hosts the heads of arabic language departments in african universities. umm al-qura university in mecca the ennobled is organising this forum, the first of its kind, in the period from last saturday, 10 rabi' al-thani 1433 ah, corresponding to 3 march 2012, up to 19 rabi' al-thani, corresponding to 12 march of the present month.

this scholarly forum was distinguished by the lecture of sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew at a scholarly symposium held on the evening of last sunday, 11 rabi' al-thani, corresponding to 4 march of the present month, under the title "the effect of colonialism in westernising the african tongue and cutting it off from the wellsprings of islamic culture".

we note that the forum runs for four days and comprises a scholarly programme taking in the academic sessions, the symposia and the workshops, and is then followed by the training programme, which runs for five consecutive days and concludes with the closing session and the recommendations.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures to the Young Woman's Association on the Anniversary of Independence on 'The Concept of Citizenship and Its Constituents'
a: الشيخ الددو يحاضر لجمعية الفتاة في ذكرى الاستقلال عن "مفهوم المواطنة ومقوماتها"
b:
the young woman's association for awareness-raising and combating school dropout hosted yesterday evening, 14 muharram 1434 ah, corresponding to (the fifty-second anniversary of the national independence day) — 28 november 2012, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew (may god preserve him) for an important lecture he delivered under the title 'the concept of citizenship and its constituents', amid a heavy turnout of hundreds of young people, women, elders and children who packed the sides of the knowledge lecture hall at the faculty of law and economics of the university of nouakchott.

at the beginning of his lecture the sheikh spoke of a person's bond with his homeland and his care for its lofty national principles and its highest values, which represent his humanity, citing in this elevated and illuminating examples from the guidance of the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and his love for his original homeland, 'medina the illuminated', from which he was driven out by force; whenever the houses of medina came into his view he would say, 'that is ṭaybah, and good it is…', and he said, 'o god, make medina beloved to us as we love mecca, and more so…'

sheikh al-dedew praised the contribution of mauritanians to the resistance against the coloniser, and mentioned prominent instances of the forms of resistance that confronted french colonialism when it entered mauritania, bringing out its cultural, religious and military varieties. the sheikh took up important subjects in this lecture, among which we mention:

• emphasising the importance of the unity of the people of a single homeland

• emphasising the importance of aspiring to honour and dignity

• urging students to strive to raise their scholarly and cultural level

• combating school dropout

• among the requirements of citizenship is the encouragement of outstanding scholarly talent in the universities

• among the rights of citizenship is a person's awareness of his duties and his rights

• political work that rests on raising awareness and on contending in the way that is best

• concern for national unity is a demand of the sharia, of the nation and of morality

• the exclusion of other parties is rejected in politics

• among the things that matter in citizenship is that people equip themselves with beneficial, useful and effective forms of knowledge, such as media work…

• among what the spirit of citizenship requires is striving for change and reform in everything

• an example of this is a magnificent poem on the prayer for rain by shaykh muhammad al-mami

• the requirements of sound citizenship, by way of shaykh muhammad al-mami's poem on the prayer for rain

• in the course of his talk sheikh al-dedew praised the role played by the scholars, the emirs and the general public in the cultural resistance and the resistance of jihad against the coloniser

• supplication

at the end of the lecture his eminence the sheikh (may god preserve him) thanked the association for its effort in raising the generations upon a sound islamic upbringing, and in striving for their educational and moral distinction, praying that god grant success to those who run the association.

to follow the lecture in the islamic thought section, click here.

t: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures at the Higher Institute on 'The Islamic Economy and Its Role in Development'
a: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يحاضر بالمعهد العالي عن "الاقتصاد الإسلامي ودوره في التنمية"
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, president of the future association for calling people to islam (daʿwah), culture and education, and president of abdullah ibn yasin university, delivered an important scholarly lecture this morning, sunday 18 muharram 1434 ah, corresponding to 02 december 2012, at the higher institute for islamic studies and research, under the title 'the islamic economy… and its role in development', at ten o'clock in the morning.

the lecture was organised as part of a scholarly symposium supervised by the fourth-year students of the islamic economics division

the lecture took place before a large student audience that packed the sides of the lecture hall, and it continued for an hour and a half.

the site will publish the lecture — god willing — shortly.

to follow the lecture, click here.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Receives the President of the Ennahda Movement, Rached Ghannouchi, at the Centre for the Formation of Scholars
a: الشيخ الددو يستقبل رئيس حركة النهضة راشد الغنوشي في مركز تكوين العلماء
b:
the erudite scholar sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, received yesterday evening, thursday 08 safar 1434 ah, corresponding to 21 december 2012, the president of the tunisian ennahda movement and islamic thinker rached ghannouchi

receiving the president of the ennahda movement were his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, the centre's director-general dr muhammad al-mukhtar ould muhammad al-mami, and a company of scholars and administrators from the centre and from outside it.

while they rested in the reception hall, an introductory presentation was given about the centre and about some of the educational and development projects it sponsors. the meeting also took in cordial conversation and the prospects for, and means of, cooperation in drawing on the long and pioneering experience of the tunisian islamic ennahda movement.

sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew accompanied shaykh rached ghannouchi on a tour of the various facilities of the centre for the formation of scholars, where the two visited the centre's library, its administrative offices, the students' residence and the centre's refectory. they also inspected at close hand the new premises for teaching the women scholars' department and the preparatory departments, both of which were opened for the first time at the beginning of the current academic year.

during the tour they made across the roofs of the buildings, the two cast an eye over the construction work on the new mosque beside the centre, which will soon, by god's power, be the great congregational mosque, holding hundreds of thousands of worshippers. the centre's administration also intends, once the new mosque is completed, to convert the present mosque building into an open traditional teaching circle (maḥẓarah) and a public library, both attached to the centre.

the president of the tunisian ennahda movement, rached ghannouchi, gave an official statement to the centre's media office shortly after the tour he made in the company of sheikh al-dedew and the accompanying delegation, in which he said that he praises god the exalted for visiting 'this achievement that god has brought about at the hands of the erudite scholar sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew', adding that sheikh al-dedew, through the centre for the formation of scholars, 'has demonstrated that there is a contemporary renewal within islam, and that within contemporary islam there is a revival of islamic civilisation,

ghannouchi added that shinqit, the capital of islamic civilisation, is renewing itself today by way of this landmark, particularly as it has taken upon itself a great trust (amānah) and a great honour: the honour of renewing islamic learning, and of contemporary renewal for the raising up of a modern class of scholars, equipped with the foundations of islam and with what contemporary modernity has produced by way of technical means for renewing the sciences and the branches of knowledge.'

shaykh ghannouchi held that mauritania, by way of the centre for the formation of scholars, demonstrates that it is 'the settled home of islamic civilisation and the settled home of the religious sciences — in maliki jurisprudence, in legal theory, in hadith and in letters'.

shaykh ghannouchi praised what he described as 'the ambition that drove sheikh muhammad al-hasan to bring forth a modern and contemporary islamic scholarship', renewing his congratulations to mauritania 'on this landmark and on this renewal'.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Receives a Shield from the Egyptian Cultural Centre in Appreciation of His Scholarly Efforts
a: الشيخ الددو يتسلم درعا من المركز الثقافي المصري تقديرا لجهوده العلمية
b:
the egyptian cultural centre in nouakchott hosted yesterday evening, sunday 11 safar 1434 ah, corresponding to 24 december 2012, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew (may god preserve him) for an important lecture organised by the centre as part of the activities of the book fair that the egyptian cultural centre is currently holding in nouakchott. the lecture took up the subject of 'the merit of knowledge'.

sheikh al-dedew praised the role of the egyptian cultural centre in spreading learning and islamic and arabic culture in mauritania over the decades, pointing out that its library used to be a focal point for visitors and a destination for young people thirsty for reading, in the days when it was the only library in the capital nouakchott.

at the end of the lecture, the chargé d'affaires at the egyptian embassy presented the sheikh with a commemorative shield from the egyptian embassy in nouakchott, in acknowledgement of his noble efforts in spreading the religious sciences and authentic islamic culture.

before that, the sheikh went round the 'egyptian book fair' held at the centre itself, bought several books, and promised the body organising the fair that he would send them copies of his own works to be distributed at the fair.

the site will publish the lecture — god willing — shortly.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Delivers an Address at the Opening of the Shinqit Centre for Islamic Finance at the Khaima Hotel
a: الشيخ الددو يلقي كلمة في افتتاح مركز شنقيط للمالية الإسلامية بفندق الخيمة
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of abdullah ibn yasin university, delivered an address at the opening of the shinqit centre for islamic finance, whose launch was announced today, tuesday 12 safar 1434 ah, corresponding to 25 december 2012

the opening proceedings were attended by a large gathering of staff of the islamic financial houses and the mauritanian banks, senior directors in particular, and by businessmen with an interest in islamic finance.

in his address at the opening of the centre, the sheikh took up the setting out of the pressing need for centres and studies of this kind, and that it has come to fill a large gap in islamic transactions (muʿāmalāt). he made clear that those running the centre want it to be an accredited international centre in the affairs of the islamic economy, and the sheikh mentioned that the banking scene in mauritania is seeing a large influx of local and international islamic banks.

the sheikh mentioned that the importance of this kind of centre requires the presence of thinkers and of people with experience in the field of sharia supervision, making clear that this centre will be careful to be in conformity with the law and disciplined by what the sharia requires, and that it will seek to reduce risk in its banking transactions and to cut back the profit returns on transactions…

the ceremony included addresses by representatives of the banks and islamic financial houses in mauritania, among them an address by the director of the bank of sound transactions (islamic), and an address by the director of the national bank for islamic transactions…

it is worth noting that this centre is sponsored by abdullah ibn yasin university and is run by a select group of professors and doctors distinguished in the religious sciences generally and in islamic finance in particular, including endowments (waqf) and zakat, alongside specialists in islamic economics, accountancy and law, foremost among them his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of abdullah ibn yasin university.

this centre aims to serve islamic finance through training, qualification, research, publication, supervision, auditing, review, and sharia and legal consultancy, and to find and develop sharia-compliant alternatives to usurious (ribā-based) transactions in the financial field.

also among its aims is to encourage usurious financial institutions to convert safely into institutions that keep within what is lawful (ḥalāl).

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in the Union's Board of Trustees Meeting as a Member and as Chair of the Membership Committee
a: الشيخ الددو يشارك في اجتماع مجلس أمناء الاتحاد بوصفه عضوا ورئيسا للجنة العضوية
b:
sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, took part in the fourth meeting of the board of trustees of the international union of muslim scholars, in its third term 2010–2014, held in the city of doha on 2–3 safar 1434 ah, corresponding to 15–16 december 2012.

sheikh al-dedew takes part as a member of the board and as chair of the membership committee. the meeting continued for two days, in which the board discussed the annual plans, the budgets and current developments, and in which they also discussed many administrative and structural matters and examined ways of remedying a number of the issues and problems of the islamic world.

thirty-seven members from various countries of the islamic world took part in the meeting.

after discussing the set agenda and deliberating on the matters put before the meeting, over two full days, the board issued a number of decisions and recommendations covering all the matters current on the islamic scene, setting out its view on each of the cases presented at the meeting.

to see further detail on the subject, please visit the website of the international union of muslim scholars at the following link:

http://www.iumsonline.net/ar/default.asp?contentid=5376&menuid=6

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures on 'The Distinctive Qualities of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and of His Community' in Ksar
a: الشيخ الددو يحاضر عن "خصائص الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأمته" بلكصر
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, delivered yesterday evening, saturday 07 rabiʿ al-awwal 1434 ah, corresponding to 19 january 2013, at the bedah mosque in the district of ksar, an important lecture on 'the distinctive qualities of the messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and of his community', which lasted two hours and saw a striking turnout of men and women, so that the congregational mosque was packed and the roads leading to it were blocked

the lecture took up the following subjects:

*- god the exalted's choosing of his messenger (peace and blessings be upon him).

*- and the most prominent distinctive qualities with which he, glorified and exalted, singled him out, such as the greater, the lesser and the intermediate intercession,

and the distinctive qualities of his community: they are the last [in time], the foremost on the day of resurrection; their work is little and their reward is multiplied…

during the lecture the sheikh spoke about the ranks of bearing witness, and about the things that draw love, which he confined to: beauty, doing good, character, hope and relationship — and how these came together in the messenger of god (peace and blessings be upon him)

he went on at length with stories about love for him (peace and blessings be upon him)… affirming that turning to god the exalted is a final remedy for poverty and need.

sheikh al-dedew explained that those who call people to god the exalted are the heirs of the prophets, and that it is honour enough for the last of this community that god the exalted says: { and others of them who have not yet joined them } (sūrat al-jumuʿah 62:3)

and that the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to his companions: 'you are in a time in which whoever falls short of a tenth of what he is commanded will perish; and a time will come upon people in which whoever brings a tenth of what he is commanded will be saved.'

- the sheikh led those present in the night prayer (ʿishāʾ), and called for the crowding in the rows to be eased, holding that with such severe crowding the prayer cannot be performed as it is required to be — which led many to go out and pray outside the mosque!

after the prayer he answered the questions of those present, and closed with a comprehensive and moving supplication…

t: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew on a Visit to the Sister State of Libya
a: فضيلة الشيخ الددو في زيارة لدولة ليبيا الشقيقة
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, made in the course of the past week an extended visit to the sister state of libya. the visit took in some of the islamic centres in libya, as well as meetings with some senior officials and the friday prayer at the murad agha mosque in tajoura.

the sheikh was received by his eminence the mufti, shaykh al-sadiq bin abd al-rahman al-ghariani, in his office at the house of fatwa (dār al-iftāʾ) in tripoli on the morning of thursday (7 march 2013), in a cordial meeting in which the two reviewed the most important current developments in the region and the means of cooperation for the sake of raising up the condition of the community.

in a meeting that brought him together with the governor of the central bank of libya, 'al-sadiq al-kabir', on thursday morning (7 march) at the headquarters of the central bank of libya in tripoli, the member of the international union of muslim scholars, shaykh 'muhammad al-hasan al-dedew', affirmed the necessity of quickening the pace towards achieving libyan economic stability and of managing its momentum, because it is — as he described it — a priority that contributes to the stability of the country generally, through cooperation between the institutions of the state and its ministries.

the meeting was an occasion on which the sheikh discussed with the officials of the central bank the islamic banking project launched in the recent period, where the erudite scholar muhammad al-hasan al-dedew affirmed the soundness of this serious transition and its positive effect on libyan life and the libyan economy generally, if it is applied in the right way.

in addition to this, sheikh al-dedew made a visit to the ministry of endowments (awqāf) in the interim transitional government, in which he met the minister charged with the ministry, the ministry's deputy, and a number of directors and heads of departments within the ministry. the meeting took up the activating of the role of mosques in libya, particularly in the process of building and of raising awareness that the phase of transition in libya requires.

al-dedew stressed the necessity of maintaining contact with all the intellectual orientations and parties in libya, and of extensive scholarly dialogue and discussion between the scholars and the students of knowledge, as well as of inviting scholars and jurists from all the islamic countries and widening the circle of contact with the world and with islamic ideas and figures.

during the evening period of thursday, sheikh al-dedew delivered a lecture at four o'clock in the afternoon at the waddan hotel in tripoli, in which he spoke of the challenges facing the renaissance of the community.

in a related context, his eminence the sheikh delivered the friday sermon at the 'murad agha mosque – in tajoura', and affirmed in it the importance of unity and agreement among all the components of the libyan people, for the sake of an effective contribution to the building of libya, and thereby the laying of a brick in the great edifice of the muslim community.

t: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew on a Visit to the State of Kuwait
a: فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو في زيارة لدولة الكويت
b:
sheikh muhammad al-hasan bin al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, is making a visit to kuwait. during this visit the sheikh delivered a valuable lecture within the proceedings of the kuwait international prize for the memorisation of the noble qur'an, in coordination with the kuwaiti ministry of endowments.

the lecture, which was broadcast live on the kuwaiti channel 'ithraa', was one in which the sheikh spoke at length,

about the majestic meanings with which the book of god abounds. he also spoke of the lofty standing this book occupies, being the summation and the seal of the revealed books…

his eminence the sheikh also touched on the meanings and the divine outpourings gathered by those who occupy themselves with this book — in study, in recitation and in reflection. the sheikh mentioned that this qur'an holds between its two covers a remedy for every intractable disease of this age, and that this has been tested: whoever has known it has known it, and whoever has been ignorant of it has been ignorant of it. the sheikh mentioned how the righteous forebears, among the companions and the generation that followed them, dealt with this qur'an

because they understood its reality and its standing — citing as an example the rightly-guided caliph umar ibn al-khattab (may god be pleased with him), who would halt at the book of god. by this qur'an, the sheikh says, god's companionship is attained, mercies descend, and souls and bodies are healed. he mentioned the story of usayd ibn hudayr (may god be pleased with him) that appears in the two ṣaḥīḥ collections, and the saying of the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to him: 'that was the tranquillity (sakīnah) that descended for the qur'an.'

in a related context, the association of the mauritanian community in the state of kuwait organised a symposium under the title:

'expatriates and the opportunities available', enlivened by a company of distinguished scholars, namely:

sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew; muhammad abd al-rahman ould ahmad, known as 'ould fata'; and his eminence the reciter and imam shaykhna ould sidi al-hajj.

t: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Lectures at the Brotherhood Season
a: فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن يحاضر في موسم الأخوة
b:
the president of the centre for the formation of scholars, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, delivered a lecture at the brotherhood season organised by the 'hand in hand' association. the subject of the lecture was under the title 'ethnic diversity'. the sheikh made clear that life is a stage for the struggle between truth and falsehood, and that the wisdom (ḥikmah) of god, glorified be he, has determined that this life should rest upon diversity and disparity between people — but that this disparity is temporary, belonging to the life of this world.

the sheikh reviewed the texts that urge the building of the bonds of brotherhood and love between muslims, and that warn in explicit terms against every form of severance and mutual aversion, so as to close off any gap or breach through which satan might enter to stir up discord (fitnah) and disagreement among the believers.

the sheikh recalled the measures that the sharia has taken for the safety of muslim society from dangers and discord, in that it has forbidden (ḥarām) backbiting, rancour, injustice, disparagement, the trading of insulting nicknames, and mockery — seeking thereby to preserve familiarity and love between muslims and to block the way before every occasion of discord and rupture. these lofty directives are what sūrat al-ḥujurāt contains, where they were a constitution upon which the muslim society in medina the illuminated was founded.

the sheikh affirmed that this brotherhood is what the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) relied upon in establishing the state in medina, in that he built the mosque and after it made a bond of brotherhood between the muslims — so much so that they used to inherit from one another on the basis of this brotherhood, before it was abrogated (mansūkh).

his eminence shaykh al-qadi bâ muhammad al-bashir commented on sheikh muhammad al-hasan's lecture, affirming that people end upon two paths and no third: the path of the god-conscious and the path of the criminals, and that it is the human being who determines his own path — 'either to a garden or to a fire'.

t: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Lectures on Moral Values in Islamic Financial Houses
a: الشيخ محمد الحسن ..يحاضر عن القيم الخلقية في المصارف الإسلامية
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, general supervisor of the shinqit centre for islamic finance, delivered today, monday 13-05-2013, a lecture on moral values in islamic financial houses. the sheikh reviewed the standing of moral character in islam, in that the qur'anic verses and the prophetic reports overflow with the commendation of character and with emphasis upon it, affirming that no civilisation and no human structure has ever stood except upon the basis of this value; and that even the people of the age of ignorance (jāhiliyyah) had moral standards they agreed upon, which were an object of praise and approval — and islam came and refined them, gave them direction, and placed in them contents and conceptions that elevate the human being and raise his worth.

his eminence the sheikh affirmed that these moral standards are part of the inheritance of prophethood, of which every muslim is bound to have a portion and a share, and that they are likewise what guarantees any success in a responsibility a person takes on: humility, forbearance, generosity and gentleness are moral qualities that cannot be dispensed with by anyone who assumes an office, or takes charge of a family, or manages an institution.

his eminence the sheikh cautioned that the character of fidelity, truthfulness and trustworthiness (amānah) is the only guarantee for the building of confidence and credibility. institutions must not announce projects that are not real, nor services that do not exist. breaching a promise and one's undertakings is not acceptable, given the speed of dealing today: being minutes late in settling a sum, for example, has become consequential, because the wheel of development turns at an extraordinary pace and speed, and precision in appointments and undertakings is the most important element in building confidence and in the success of institutions.

sheikh muhammad al-hasan mentioned basic rules for the success of any economic undertaking, which he drew from the report of uthman (may god be pleased with him) and from the counsel of qarun's people — for these two texts are to be regarded as a constitution and a moral charter upon which any sound economic undertaking rests.

among these rules: 'treatment; development'; attention to profit; avoiding old stock and goods past their validity; adopting the policy of not putting the eggs in one basket, that is, of breaking up capital; and likewise seeking the abode of the hereafter in any work, and doing good, and not seeking corruption in the earth — which is a comprehensive sense that takes in the selling of defective goods, falsification, hoarding, and taking on debts that cannot be repaid, for all of that falls under the name of 'corruption in the earth'.

the sheikh closed by saying that the economy is a ladder by which culture and civilisation ascend, and that it must therefore be free of every kind of cheating, betrayal and deception.

after that the sheikh answered the questions of those present, which were closely tied to the subject of transactions (muʿāmalāt) and islamic financial houses, and of the alternative forms to conventional transactions.

it is worth noting that this lecture was held at the tfeila hotel in the mauritanian capital nouakchott, within the proceedings of the training course organised by the shinqit centre for islamic finance, attached to abdullah ibn yasin university, in cooperation with the bank of sound transactions.

sheikh al-dedew, general supervisor of the shinqit centre for islamic finance, had delivered an address at the opening session of the course yesterday.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in a Symposium: A Reading of 'The Inspiration of the Maḥẓarah' (by the Poet Yeslem Ould Akibed)
a: الشيخ الددو يشارك في ندوة: قراءة في إلهام المحظرة (للشاعر يسلم ولد أكيبد)
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars and president of the future association for upbringing, culture and education, delivered an address of commendation and tribute at the ceremony held by the union of mauritanian writers and authors for the signing and the study of the poetry collection (dīwān) of the man of letters yeslem ould akibed, which was gathered and studied by dr al-hasan ould akibed. the ceremony was held at the khatir hotel on the evening of monday 13 may 2013.

in his address sheikh al-dedew paid tribute to the collection of the poet yeslem ould akibed and to the abundance of his learning and letters, giving an account of the poet's origins and life and of the stages of his education between the two traditional teaching circles (maḥẓarah) of ahl adud and ahl yahzih ould abd al-wadud. sheikh al-dedew also spoke of a companionship that had joined him to the man of letters ould akibed, pointing out that he was among the outstanding minds of the maḥẓarah school; that he was known for his devotion in worship and his indifference to fame, for which reason he used to conceal his poetry and would not consent to its being published or recited, and rarely recited any of it even when people pressed him; that his poetry gave expression to his region and his age; and that he was the descendant of a righteous family and a god-fearing house, his mother being among the god-fearing and scrupulous women — and this descent from two righteous parents left a clear mark on his character and his upbringing.

sheikh al-dedew pointed out that the late man of letters ould akibed engaged in poetic exchanges with his contemporaries and was a model of the formation of the 'lebyarat' region, expressing the wish that the poet's hassaniya collection would find its way to publication, as a collection no less important than his classical arabic one.

there followed contributions from the audience of writers and intellectuals taking part in the symposium, all of which concluded with the creative, cultural and historical importance of this collection in particular, and of the mauritanian maḥẓarah in general.

taking part in this ceremony was a select company of writers, poets and thinkers, among them the man of letters abdullah al-salem ould al-moalla, the poet and man of letters ahmedou ould abdel kader, the man of letters naji muhammad al-imam, the lawyer mohameden ould ichidou, and the prince of poets muhammad ould al-talib… and a large gathering of writers and intellectuals.

t: Replies to the Questions Sent to the Site, Part 3
a: ردود على الأسئلة الواردة على الموقع ج3
b:
the question: our noble and excellent shaykh,

peace be upon you, and the mercy of god the exalted, and his blessings.

shaykh al-huwayni mentioned a set of prophetic reports, describing some of them as weak (ḍaʿīf) and others as void. we hope that you will make clear to us the soundness of that, for according to the knowledge we have taken from you, weakness and soundness are not a matter of certainty — as al-hafiz al-iraqi said: by 'sound' and 'weak' they intended a judgement upon what is apparent, not certainty. so instruct us, may god instruct you.

----------------------------

the answer:

in the name of god, the most merciful, the compassionate.

praise be to god, lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace upon our prophet muhammad and upon his family and his companions all together.

to proceed. the reports that shaykh abu ishaq al-huwayni mentioned include fabricated ones (mawḍūʿ) whose fabrication is certain; and they include weak reports (ḍaʿīf) whose falsity is not certain; and they include traditions whose tracing to the prophet (rafʿ) is void but which are sound as reports stopping at a companion (mawqūf) or stopping at a follower (maqṭūʿ). an example of this is: 'the black stone is the right hand of the merciful on earth' — its tracing to the prophet is void, but it is sound as a report stopping at ibn abbas, without the addition to which the shaykh referred. and an example of the weak whose falsity is not held to be certain, and over whose grade there has been disagreement, is: 'the most hateful of the permitted things to god is divorce' — the people of knowledge have mentioned constructions of it that answer the objection the shaykh raised against its text (matn). as for the report 'the full moon rose over us', the objection the shaykh has raised against it is not to be conceded, for in medina there are two mountain passes: a pass near quba on the rise of the ḥarrah, which is the southern thaniyyat al-wadaʿ; and the other on the northern side of salʿ, which has now been demolished and of which no trace remains, which is the northern thaniyyat al-wadaʿ. and the objection that the word 'al-thaniyyāt' comes in the plural form is answered by the fact that the arabs put a place in the plural together with what surrounds it, and that is well known in the language. likewise the report: 'pray behind every righteous man and every transgressor', and in another wording: 'behind whoever says: there is no god but god' — they disagreed over holding it to be weak, and among the people of knowledge are those who apply it to the funeral prayer. and god knows best.

-------------------

the question: i found an advertisement on the internet for the sale of a plot of land at a price that suited me. i called the mobile number and asked about the land, whether it was still offered for sale. the estate agency (let us call it agency 1) informed me that it was still offered for sale and that nobody had bought it.

i made an appointment with agency 1 for the same day, and when i arrived at agency 1 the landowner's authorised agent called me; and after speaking with him it became clear to me that the land had been offered through another estate agency (let us call it agency 2) — that is, the same land was offered through two agencies at one and the same time.

the authorised agent told me that someone had paid a deposit (ʿurbūn) to agency 2 before i paid my deposit. so i told the authorised agent that i had the amount available in cash, and that the choice in the end was theirs.
