and this is not lawful in cases other than the like of these, because this belongs to the rulings of necessity (ḍarūrah). and if it is possible for the imam, the muezzin and a third with them to pray in the mosque, and for the imam to deliver the sermon to them, then there is no objection to its being transmitted over the mosque's network, or its radio, or the loudspeaker, and to people praying it at a distance in their homes, or in their shops, or in their offices, hearing the sermon by way of the loudspeaker or the radio of the mosque's network; for it suffices them too, when they are prevented from attending and prevented from entering the mosque — because when the mosque is too narrow, the friday prayer is valid in the roads connected to it, and in its forecourt, and in places where it is feasible for them to pray. on this question there is a detailed treatment which the jurists give, in which they mention four cases:

- if the mosque is too narrow and the rows are connected, there is no disagreement as to its soundness and its permissibility in the roads and the forecourt, and likewise in the houses near the mosque.

- if the mosque is spacious and the rows are not connected, the majority of them hold it not to be allowed, contrary to the narration of ibn shaʿban in the maliki school.

- if the mosque is spacious and the rows are connected, then it is void, contrary to ashhab among the malikis.

- if the mosque is too narrow and the rows are not connected, then on this question there is disagreement, on three positions:

1 — the soundness of the friday prayer;

2 — the voidness of the friday prayer;

3 — the soundness of the friday prayer together with its being disliked.

in general, what is taken from this is that people may pray in their homes if they are prevented from the mosques, and may follow the imam by his voice if they hear it, whether that be by loudspeaker, or by the radio of the mosque's network, or the like; and those further away may listen to the sermon and benefit from it.

may god honour you, prot

t: The Ruling on Refraining from Cutting the Hair and Nails During the Ten Days of Dhu al-Hijjah
a: حكم الكف عن قص الشعر و الأظافر في عشر ذي الحجة
b:
as for one who has no eid sacrifice (uḍḥiyah), and for the members of a household on whose behalf the one who supports them will be sacrificing, it is permissible for them to cut their hair and their nails whenever they wish, by the agreement of the scholars.

as for one who intends to perform the sacrifice himself, the jurists have differed over him between forbiddenness, dislikedness and permissibility:

the hanbalis and some of the shafi'is held that it is forbidden (ḥarām) for him to cut his hair or his nails until he has slaughtered his sacrificial animal.

the hanafis held that it is permissible (jāʾiz) for him to do so, without its being disliked.

the malikis and the shafi'is held that it is disliked (makrūh) for him, and that refraining from cutting the hair and the nails is recommended (mandūb) and not obligatory (wājib).

the basis of this is what imam muslim narrated from umm salamah (may god be pleased with her), that the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "when you see the crescent of dhu al-hijjah, and one of you intends to sacrifice, let him refrain from his hair and his nails"; and in another narration: "let him not cut any hair nor clip any nail."

this is a prohibitive command, and a prohibitive command, when it does not entail forbiddenness, is taken to convey dislikedness. sheikh khalil said: "and it is recommended (nadb) for one who is to sacrifice to leave off shaving and clipping during the ten days of dhu al-hijjah." it is recommended only in order to resemble the pilgrim.

the malikis and the shafi'is argued that the prohibition conveys dislikedness and not forbiddenness by what imam malik and the two sheikhs [al-bukhari and muslim] narrated from aisha (may god be pleased with her), who said: "i plaited the garlands of the messenger of god's sacrificial camels with my own hands; then he marked them and garlanded them, then sent them to the house while he himself stayed in medina, and nothing that had been lawful for him became forbidden to him"; and in another narration: "then he (peace and blessings be upon him) sent them with my father" — that is, with abu bakr (may god be pleased with him), in the ninth year of the hijrah.

its meaning is: nothing of the prohibited acts of the consecrated state of pilgrimage (iḥrām) became forbidden to him — not women, nor perfume, nor removing dishevelment, nor shaving the hair, nor clipping the nails, nor anything else of what god has made lawful…

and god knows best.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew’s Commendation of the Book Irshad al-Maharah fi Asanid al-Mahdarah by the Learned Shaykh Muhammad Yahzih ibn Muhammad Ali
a: تقريظ  الشيخ الددو لكتاب إرشاد المهرة  في أسانيد المحضرة للشيخ العلامة محمد يحظيه بن محمد عالي
b:
sheikh al-dedew's commendation of the book *irshad al-maharah fi asanid al-mahdarah* by the learned shaykh muhammad yahzih ibn muhammad ali.

the commendation of the eminent sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew of the book *irshad al-maharah fi asanid al-mahdarah*, by the eminent and learned shaykh muhammad yahzih ibn muhammad ali ibn muhammad fal ibn naam al-abd al-majlisi.

[verse. rendered as prose, line by line; the arabic is the operative text.]

*a noble book, exalted in the world of books, which broke new ground in the history of the western flank,*

*and closed a gap that stood in our libraries, by joining up the chains of transmission (asānīd) of the traditional schools and of the books,*

*and spread out again what the long passage of time had folded away and buried of the traces of its conquering lions,*

*and guided the skilled and the rightly directed to the most profitable ways of travelling in the track of the caravan.*

*by it the shaykh, the imam, brought to light wonders at which one marvels — wonders that guide, and that cure a man of marvelling.*

*muhammad yahzih, the noble, is our lamp, first past the post in the race of knowledge across the wide and open waste,*

*the halting-place where students unload their mounts, one practised at laying the tar-salve exactly where the mange is,*

*such that in him knowledge, understanding and god-consciousness (taqwā) stand side by side with generosity and good character,*

*together with an elevated literary art, finely turned verse, and a refined taste that never strays from the road —*

*all of it joined to a lineage of towering honour and glory, risen from noble stock by the steep ascent.*

*abu ahmad, the noble and ready man, was their father; glory has been passed down from him, ready man to ready man.*

*their breasts were created as vessels for understanding, and their lifetimes for occupation with the obligatory (farḍ) and the recommended (nadb);*

*their feet for outstripping others on the paths of eminence, and their hands for giving, for enquiry and for writing.*

*in glory, honour and eminence they have reached the furthest ranks, not to be approached even by the noblest of men;*

*and in the awe-inspiring assembly of learning they took the middle place, at a forefront where they stood as the heart stands.*

*at the dome of islam is the stronghold of their honour, under a lucky star and in a spacious dwelling.*

*so too the house of naam al-abd have been a blessing to people, level-spread in their hospitality, like a sweet watering place:*

*obeyed in the thick of battle, lamps in the darkness, keys to what is locked, deliverers from distress.*

*and this shaykh follows his father in his qualities, matching him in every title to glory, or surpassing him.*

*time has begrudged the world the like of his writings; their precedence is assured, far and near.*

*it is as though abu hayyan meant his books by the lines he spoke in al-bahr wa-l-darb:*

*"easterly risings of lights that shone forth at ceuta — and what a wonder, that the risings should appear in the west!"*

*a fertile pasture amid the barrenness of its lands — marvel, then, at fertility in the place of drought!*

*for regions have no merit except through their men; failing that, no soil has any merit over soil.*

t: A Welcome to Mauritania’s Guest, al-Sayyid al-Mustafa ibn al-Imam al-Shafiʻi
a: ترحيب بضيف موريتانيا السيد المصطفى بن الإمام الشافعي
b:
[verse. rendered as prose, line by line; the arabic is the operative text.]

*my country bids welcome to the noble and beneficent one, al-mustafa, son of the imam al-shafi'i,*

*to the eloquent one, the valiant and resolute champion, the well-pleasing, possessed of honour and of high and far-spread renown,*

*the close companion of manliness, of noble deeds and high aspiration, of open-handedness and of fine and splendid character;*

*one who comes to the aid of the wronged without hesitation, and looses the bonds of the abject soul who calls for help.*

*in his favours and his gifts he makes no distinction between the importunate and the chaste and contented man:*

*each receives his share of his bounty, with a cheerful face, with affection and with humility.*

*he inherited these noble qualities from forefathers of honour, whose eminence spread through the widest reaches.*

*the noble ones of the line of jakar have hedged their titles to glory about with a broad edifice;*

*their present state points back to their past, and their past points forward to this present state.*

*they are the buyers of every noble quality and every height, and they bid the price up high for the seller.*

*knowledge is in them, and courage, and right guidance, and generosity, together with a widely known nobility of soul —*

*an inheritance passed down through the length of time, its hardships and all, from the one followed to the one who follows.*

*jakan are the pillars of the sciences, the qiblah of the wronged, his place of safety and the honour of the lowly.*

*their honour is inviolable and guarded, and their goods are apportioned out like things held in trust.*

*in every age they raise up for our people a banner of knowledge, pointed to like a shining star.*

*so may god grant them victory, and keep your memory alive, and make their favour endure in unbroken good.*

t: Sheikh al-Dedew’s Elegy for Shaykh al-Din ibn Muhammad Ali ibn Takrur
a: مرثية الشيخ الددو للشيخ الدين بن محمد علي ابن تكرور
b:
[verse. rendered as prose, line by line; the arabic is the operative text.]

*is it truly al-din whose death you have announced — he of religion and right guidance, of knowledge and character, of glory and open-handedness;*

*he of the well-pleasing way, and of those sunnah practices for which he held a chain of transmission going back to the messenger of god;*

*defending them, repudiating every innovation in religion (bidʿah), and no faint-heart, however many the enemies grew;*

*he who among us took the lead in understanding and in quickness of mind, and who among us ran the whole course in his noble deeds;*

*who put knowledge and mastery into the hands of generations, and so accustomed them to it that it became their habit;*

*who was a ready man, eloquent of speech, foremost in place, honoured, firmly established, a chief among his clan,*

*high-minded, upright, his honour never to be slighted; a doer, a speaker, upholding what is right.*

*if al-din has departed from us, following after his companions, and has left a numbing grief in our souls —*

*then he has not died who has left his sons and his household behind him, and he has not died who has left a praise that endures.*

*so take patience, noble sons of musa, our shaykhs and our masters: may every one of us be your ransom.*

*may you never cease to be a wellspring of religion and knowledge, and a watering place of generosity, character and honour.*

*our beloved ones, o house of amina, be patient: al-din among you is not one man — he is many.*

*you remain for us a cave of refuge, a strength and a haven, and for religion, character and knowledge a root stock.*

*may my lord lodge al-din in the noblest of lodgings, and place his record in his right hand tomorrow,*

*and settle him in the highest garden as a neighbour to his forefather, the messenger of guidance — how true a seat is that!*

*and may my god bless his sons and their mother, and his two daughters; and may he keep them, honour them and give them happiness.*

*and may he send blessings upon the best of mankind, and upon his family, his companions, and the rightly guided who followed them.*

t: Sheikh al-Dedew's Prayer for the Recovery of His Eminence the Learned Sheikh Muhammad Mahmud Ahmad Yura al-Rabbani
a: استشفاء الشيخ الددو لفضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد محمود أحمد يورة الرباني
b:
o our lord, heal our sheikh muhammad

mahmud, who has traversed the farthest reach in excellence,

of the line of ahmad yura, who stood alone

in knowledge and in character, and so was without peer,

the most radiant of face and the most noble of descent,

the most truthful in speech and the most open-handed,

the finest in conduct and the highest in chain of transmission,

the purest of heart and the most exacting in purpose.

he has built a glory for the two forefathers, long inherited,

clothed in generosity, the imams of guidance.

lord, grant him what he seeks and what he aims at,

preserve him and help him with a strengthening help,

and in his sons let what has been customary continue,

that they stand, one master after another.

grant maryam the wish that will make her happy,

answer this supplication, and subdue the enemies.

t: The Ruling on Selling Imported Food Before It Reaches the Merchant's Warehouses | Fatwas of Sheikh al-Dedew
a: حكم بيع الطعام المستورد قبل وصوله مخازن التاجر | فتاوى الشيخ الددو
b:
a questioner asks about the ruling on selling imported food before it reaches the merchant's warehouses, and whether this falls under the prohibition of selling food before taking possession of it (qabḍ); and, on that basis, if he sells it and its price rises before it arrives, whether the seller may rescind the sale or raise the price.

and upon you be peace, and the mercy of god and his blessings.

as to selling food before it arrives: if it has already entered the seller's ownership and his liability (ḍamān), so that it is owned by him and is no longer owned by the company from which he bought it — as where it was he who shipped it by sea and he who insured it — then it is permissible for him to sell it, because it has come into his ownership and his possession, even if it has not reached the market, even if it has not reached the country at all, and even if it is loaded on board at sea; before it reaches the port it is permissible for him to sell it. and once he has sold it, it is not lawful for him to go back on his sale, because the sale has already taken effect, even if the price rises afterwards. for god, glorified and exalted, says: { o you who believe, fulfil your contracts } (sūrat al-māʾidah 5:1); and he says: { and those who fulfil their covenant when they make a covenant } (sūrat al-baqarah 2:177); and the glorified and exalted says: { and fulfil the covenant of god when you have made a covenant } (sūrat al-naḥl 16:91). it is established as sound from the prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "the signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted he betrays the trust" — narrated by al-bukhari. and it is established as sound from him (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "four traits: whoever has them in him is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has in him a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it — when he is entrusted he betrays the trust, when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he acts treacherously, and when he disputes he behaves depravedly" — narrated by al-bukhari.

may god protect us and you from hypocrisy, from discord and from bad character, and may he make what he has made lawful suffice us and you, so that we have no need of what he has forbidden.

and peace be upon you, and the mercy of god and his blessings.

fatwas of his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew al-shinqiti

t: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew Congratulates Sheikh Muhammad Sidiya (al-Nawawi) Ould Sulayman Ould Ajdud on the Welcome of His Beloved Son Abdullah — May God Almighty Preserve Them Both
a: قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو مهنئا الشيخ محمد سيديا (النووي) ولد سليمان ولد اجدود ترحيبا بابنه الغالي عبد الله، حفظهما الله تعالى
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew said, congratulating sheikh muhammad sidiya (al-nawawi) ould sulayman ould ajdud in welcome of his beloved son abdullah — may god almighty preserve them both:

o abdullah, live out an age that is praiseworthy,

noble, honoured, dutiful and happy.

be like your father, a scholar of every discipline,

and one who restores the sunnah practices that have fallen into disuse.

hold fast to the upright way and guard it,

and you will never swerve from the middle of the road.

recite the qur'an measuredly; that was their constant practice,

the practice of the forefathers, their long-inherited way.

may god give you of what he gave them,

and increase you in elevation and in further guidance.

be a shade for the sheikh, and gather what he has

gathered for the students, and so be of benefit.

hasten to acts of nobility and to high things,

and live in his shade a life of ease.

strive for the victory of the truth, and be brave

like your noble family, and die a martyr.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew's Congratulation to His Eminence Sheikh al-Nawawi, and the Reply of His Eminence Sheikh Abdullah Ajdud, "al-ʿAbbad"
a: تهنئة الشيخ الددو لفضيلة الشيخ النووي و جواب فضيلة الشيخ عبد الله اجدود " العباد *
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew said, congratulating sheikh muhammad sidiya (al-nawawi) ould sulayman ould ajdud in welcome of his beloved son abdullah — may god almighty preserve them both:

o abdullah, live out an age that is praiseworthy,

noble, honoured, dutiful and happy.

be like your father, a scholar of every discipline,

and one who restores the sunnah practices that have fallen into disuse.

hold fast to the upright way and guard it,

and you will never swerve from the middle of the road.

recite the qur'an measuredly; that was their constant practice,

the practice of the forefathers, their long-inherited way.

may god give you of what he gave them,

and increase you in elevation and in further guidance.

be a shade for the sheikh, and gather what he has

gathered for the students, and so be of benefit.

hasten to acts of nobility and to high things,

and live in his shade a life of ease.

strive for the victory of the truth, and be brave

like your noble family, and die a martyr.

the answer and reply of his eminence sheikh abdullah "al-ʿabbad" ibn sulayman ibn ajdud, adviser to the minister of endowments and islamic affairs in the state of qatar, to his eminence sheikh al-dedew's congratulation to the learned al-nawawi — may god almighty preserve them — was as follows:

peace be upon you, and the mercy of god and his blessings.

may god greet you, his eminence the sheikh, and preserve you and keep you.

from the moment the limpid and splendid piece of verse reached me, which you sent me as a congratulation and a supplication for our blessed son — god almighty willing — abdullah, i have been in the utmost delight and joy at it.

it has taken a place with all of us that none knows but god almighty, and we count it among the glories of this world for us, and we hope it will be among that by which the treasure of the hereafter is attained.

i have composed some verses, despite how long it has been since i last wrote poetry — perhaps more than thirty years, praise be to god — and i do not think they do it justice, nor match it in form or in meaning, nor rise to its measure. the verses are:

o abdullah, your good fortune admits of no addition

beyond what it is, so be glad and happy with it.

vaunt yourself before the gatherings of the young, since

sheikh al-dedew has prayed that you become a master.

he went to the utmost in congratulating you, and adorned

your kin with a matchless necklace of eminence.

so reward him, lord, with a good recompense, and multiply

for him, on our behalf, his reward, and add to it.

and grant him, lord, all that he hopes for,

removing from him every harm, far away.

o sheikh of sheikhs, and pride of an age

that god favoured with your glorious rising —

i forsook poetry long ago, and it is now

a duty upon me that my return to it be praiseworthy.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew's Commendation of the Book The Genealogical Tree of the Idrisids of Sidi Yahya, by the Noble Sayyid Sheikh Muhammad al-Mukhtar ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Da'im, May God Preserve Him
a: تقريظ الشيخ الددو لكتاب ( شجرة الأدارسة سيدي يحيى ) للسيد الشريف الشيخ محمد المختار بن أحمد بن عبد الدائم حفظه الله
b:
i said, in commendation of the book the genealogical tree of the idrisids of sidi yahya, by the noble sayyid, sheikh muhammad al-mukhtar ibn ahmad ibn abd al-da'im, may god preserve him:

muhammad al-mukhtar, possessor of knowledge and excellence,

of righteousness, kindness, generosity and open-handed giving;

possessor of a high and noble lineage, and of god-consciousness (taqwā),

of the most exemplary traits and of an easy disposition.

his forefathers bequeathed him every excellence,

and through his maternal uncles it was perfected, excellence upon excellence:

from the family of abd al-da'im he gained eminence,

and from the righteous family of al-zuwayn, people of nobility.

he has books that hold precious treasures,

beautiful in their arrangement, sound in what they transmit.

he has set out from the genealogies a detailed volume

that helps those of us who are kin to keep the ties of kinship.

he has given the lives of notable figures, verified attributions of descent,

made homelands clear, and enumerated the offspring.

it holds a clear account of the genealogies of tanwajiw

for their descendants, so that like is joined to like.

and he traces the branches of the pole (quṭb) sidi yahya back

to sidi idris, of original nobility,

to his father idris, of glory and eminence,

to the excellent abdullah, of merit and justice,

to al-hasan the excellent, al-muthanna, who rose to

the summits of might, of divine enabling, of forbearance and of sound judgement,

to al-hasan the grandson, son of haydara the well-pleasing,

through fatimah al-zahra, to the master of the messengers —

upon him be god's blessings without ceasing, and upon his family,

and the purest peace, joining the branch to the root.

written by muhammad al-hasan ibn al-dedew.

t: Taking In Public Lectures, Classes and Fatwa Sessions — Sheikh al-Dedew on a Da'wah Tour to the Mauritanian Region of Dakhlet Nouadhibou
a: تشمل إقامة محاضرات ودروس وحلقات إفتاء.. الشيخ الددو في رحلة دعوية إلى ولاية داخلت انواذيبو الموريتانية
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew — head of the centre for the formation of scholars, president of the al-mustaqbal association, and a member of the board of trustees of the international union of muslim scholars — delivered a scholarly lecture entitled "the factors of the ummah's strength", as part of a series of lectures and classes hosted by mauritania's economic capital, the region of dakhlet nouadhibou, which lies 470 km from the capital nouakchott.

this event comes as part of a da'wah tour in the region organised by the al-mustaqbal association for da'wah, culture and education on 25 and 26 june of this month; the tour takes in a series of lectures, classes and fatwa sessions.

these are the principal lectures, in chronological order:

in the district of chami:

* the first lecture: "lawful earning", at the al-furqan congregational mosque in the district of chami, which opened the da'wah tour.

* a fatwa session specifically for gold prospectors and those working in prospecting, in which sheikh al-dedew answered the questions of those present.

and in the district of nouadhibou:

* a lecture at the quba mosque on "coming to the prophet's aid, god bless him and grant him peace, and what that requires".

* a lecture entitled "how do we pray the prayer of the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace?", at the al-ridwan mosque. — organised by the al-furqan association for culture and upbringing.

* a lecture entitled "the factors of the ummah's strength", at the abu bakr al-siddiq congregational mosque.

* "the merit of the ten days of dhu al-hijjah", organised by the women's association for combating poverty and illiteracy.

* the duty of the muslim young woman in coming to the aid of the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace — organised by the al-fatat association for awareness and upbringing.

t: From Muhammad al-Hasan ibn al-Dedew to Every Muslim Whom This Reaches
a: من محمد الحسن بن الدَّدَوْ إلى كل من يصل إليه من المسلمين
b:
peace be upon you, and the mercy of god and his blessings.

to proceed: among the best seasons of good in the year is this season with which god has favoured you in these days of merit, which are the best days of the year. the group narrated — except muslim and al-nasa'i — from the hadith of ibn abbas, may god be pleased with them both, who said: the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, said: «there are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to god, mighty and majestic, than these days» — meaning the ten days of dhu al-hijjah. and ahmad and others narrated from the hadith of ibn umar, may god be pleased with them both, who said: the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, said: «there are no days greater in the sight of god, glorified is he, nor in which deeds are more beloved to him, than these ten days; so do much in them of declaring god's oneness, of declaring his greatness and of praising him.» so exert yourselves in righteous deeds in these days, and especially in the following:

1 - fasting all of them. ahmad and al-nasa'i narrated from hafsa bint umar, may god be pleased with them both, who said: «four things the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, did not leave: the fast of ashura, the ten days, three days of every month, and the two cycles before the morning meal.» what is meant is all but the day of eid, for fasting it is not lawful. for this reason abu dawud narrated from one of the wives of the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, who said: «the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, used to fast the nine days of dhu al-hijjah, the day of ashura, three days of every month, and the first monday of the month, and the thursdays.» as for the hadith of aisha with muslim: «i never saw the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, fasting in the ten days at all.» — that is to be understood as referring to the hajj.

2 - fasting the day of arafah in particular, for one who is not on hajj. muslim, ahmad, abu dawud and ibn majah narrated from abu qatada, may god be pleased with him, who said: the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, said: «fasting the day of arafah expiates two years, one past and one to come; and fasting the day of ashura expiates one past year.» and in another wording: «i reckon upon god that he will expiate the year before it and the year after it.»

3 - doing much remembrance of god. al-bukhari said in the ṣaḥīḥ: «and ibn abbas said: {and that they may mention the name of god on the appointed days} (sūrat al-ḥajj 22:28) — the days of the ten. he said: and ibn umar and abu hurayra used to go out to the market during the days of the ten, declaring god's greatness, and the people would declare his greatness at their declaring it.» and there has already come, in the hadith of ibn umar, the instruction to do much of declaring god's oneness, declaring his greatness and praising him.

4 - that one who is going to offer the eid sacrifice (uḍḥiyah) not take anything from his hair or his nails from the beginning of the month until he has sacrificed, in resemblance to one in the consecrated state of pilgrimage (muḥrim). the group narrated — except al-bukhari — from the hadith of umm salama, may god be pleased with her, that the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, said: «whoever has an animal to slaughter that he is going to slaughter — when the crescent of dhu al-hijjah appears, let him not take anything from his hair or his nails until he has sacrificed.»

and god grant us and you every good, and accept from us and from you.

written by muhammad al-hasan ibn al-dedew, may god be for him a protector and a helper

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Delivers an Address at the Opening of the Sixth Conference of the Kuala Lumpur Forum for Thought and Civilisation
a: الشيخ الددو يلقي كلمة في افتتاح المؤتمر السادس لمنتدى كوالالمبور للفكر والحضارة
b: this morning, 11-12-2022, in the turkish capital istanbul, the proceedings of the sixth conference of the kuala lumpur forum for thought and civilisation opened under the banner "civilisational resumption and the projects of revival in the islamic ummah (roots — present reality — future)", with the participation of his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, deputy president of the forum, his eminence dr abderrazak makri, secretary-general of the forum, and a great throng of the ummah's scholars, its thinkers and the leaders of its renaissance. the conference was opened with a fragrant recitation from the wise remembrance, followed by a video presenting the forum, then the address of the secretary-general and the address of the deputy president, and a video about the forum's achievements. the forum's secretary-general, his eminence dr abderrazak makri, gave an address in which he welcomed those attending and spoke about the foremost obstacles facing the ummah at the present time and how they are to be overcome. for his part, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, deputy president of the forum, spoke about the challenges the ummah has faced, and about what the sons of the ummah are obliged to do for the sake of its renaissance and its advancement and the repelling of injustice from it; his eminence then spoke about the fall of the caliphate, the scattering of the ummah, the occupation of its lands and the ascendancy of the western powers over it. he also called upon those who work for reform to occupy themselves with upbringing and with knowledge, with reconciling people to one another, with helping others past their stumbles, and with casting off discord. the opening ceremony also included the presentation of a number of plaques and certificates of appreciation to the figures and bodies taking part in the ummah's renaissance and the defence of its causes. the conference continues for three days, in which the participants discuss projects for the ummah's revival, so as to put forward a set of recommendations and proposals such as would raise up the ummah and contribute to its renaissance.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures in Hodh ech Chargui as Part of His Da'wah Programme in Eastern Mauritania
a: الشيخ الددو يحاضر في الحوض الشرقي ضمن برنامجه الدعوي في الشرق الموريتاني
b:
at midday yesterday, monday 11 september 2023, in the district of néma, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew delivered his fourth lecture within his eminence's da'wah programme, speaking about the muslim's responsibility towards his religion and its sanctities,
explaining that the muslim is answerable before god for the message of muhammad, god bless him and grant him peace; that he is under trial in this life; and that he is required to defend his religion and the honour of his messenger.
he affirmed that when the philosophers of the west proved unable to corrupt the muslim's creed (ʿaqīdah) and to weaken his love for his prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, and his attachment to him, they wanted him to live for his appetites, keeping away from his religion and from his relationship with his lord; and that they therefore devised a set of theories calling for the casting off of religions, for attachment to matter, for war on sound natural disposition (fiṭrah), and for the spreading of gross indecencies.
this lecture comes within the da'wah programme organised by the al-mustaqbal association for da'wah, culture and education.
this programme takes in a set of scholarly and da'wah lectures calling for the purification of the human soul (tazkiyah), urging noble character, and the necessity that a person occupy himself with what secures for him the good of both the hereafter and this life.
this programme comes within the da'wah plan of the president of the al-mustaqbal association, his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew.
his eminence had opened his da'wah programme with a lecture in the town of aghchorguitt on the evening of last saturday, 9 september 2023.
the programme included a visit of condolence to his eminence sheikh ahmad jiddou ould ahmad bahi, deputy chairman of the association's consultative council, in the village of boukhzama, which the sheikh reached on monday night before delivering two lectures to the people of the village. the first of them was on the necessity that the muslim provide himself with provision for the abode of the hereafter, citing his saying, god bless him and grant him peace, "death is sufficient as an admonisher"; and in the second lecture he urged them to preserve their values, to compete in acts of obedience, and to take as their model the master of all creation, god bless him and grant him peace.
his eminence also delivered a lecture in the town of timbedra last night, in which he spoke about the character of the muslim, and what he ought to be in this world by way of shrewdness, alertness and putting god's command first; and he went over the story of the companions of the cave and their faith in god and their sacrifice in his path, exalted is he.
the programme is expected to include further lectures in each of oualata, tintane, kiffa and kouro.

t: From Muhammad al-Hasan ibn al-Dedew to Every Muslim Whom This Reaches
a: من محمد الحسن بن الدَّدَوْ إلى كل من يصل إليه من المسلمين
b:

1 - fasting all of them. ahmad and al-nasa'i narrated from hafsa bint umar, may god be pleased with them both, who said: «four things the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, did not leave: the fast of ashura, the ten days, three days of every month, and the two cycles before the morning meal.» what is meant is all but the day of eid, for fasting it is not lawful. for this reason abu dawud narrated from one of the wives of the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, who said: «the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, used to fast the nine days of dhu al-hijjah, the day of ashura, three days of every month, and the first monday of the month, and the thursdays.» as for the hadith of aisha with muslim: «i never saw the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, fasting in the ten days at all.» — that is to be understood as referring to the hajj.
2 - fasting the day of arafah in particular, for one who is not on hajj. muslim, ahmad, abu dawud and ibn majah narrated from abu qatada, may god be pleased with him, who said: the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, said: «fasting the day of arafah expiates two years, one past and one to come; and fasting the day of ashura expiates one past year.» and in another wording: «i reckon upon god that he will expiate the year before it and the year after it.»

4 - that one who is going to offer the eid sacrifice (uḍḥiyah) not take anything from his hair or his nails from the beginning of the month until he has sacrificed, in resemblance to one in the consecrated state of pilgrimage (muḥrim). the group narrated — except al-bukhari — from the hadith of umm salama, may god be pleased with her, that the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, said: «whoever has an animal to slaughter that he is going to slaughter — when the crescent of dhu al-hijjah appears, let him not take anything from his hair or his nails until he has sacrificed.»
and god grant us and you every good, and accept from us and from you.
written by muhammad al-hasan ibn al-dedew, may god be for him a protector and a helper

t: From Nouadhibou — Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew Launches This Year's Scholarly and Da'wah Programme with Lectures on the Values of Faith and the Reform of Society
a: من نواذيبو.. الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو يطلق برنامجه العلمي والدعوي لهذا العام  بمحاضرات في القيم الإيمانية وإصلاح المجتمع
b: at midday today — tuesday 21 july 2026 — his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew launched this year's scholarly and da'wah programme from the city of nouadhibou, beginning a scholarly and guidance tour taking in public lectures, scholarly classes and da'wah meetings, within the framework of his mission of establishing islamic values, strengthening religious awareness, calling for holding fast to the book and the sunnah, and urging the virtues of character. the first day of the programme saw a wide attendance that included a number of scholars, students of knowledge, imams and callers to islam, alongside a great throng of the city's people who came to attend the sheikh's first lectures and to benefit from his scholarly classes. at the opening of his scholarly programme for this year, at the al-jawdah centre for the sharia sciences, his eminence the sheikh took up the standing of knowledge and the merit of learning and teaching it, and the urging of care for its institutions, the embracing of its students and support for those who run them — for it is everyone's responsibility — affirming that through knowledge concord is reached, brotherhood is realised, justice spreads, and god is worshipped as he has prescribed. in the second lecture, hosted by the quba congregational mosque, he took up the factors of the soundness of society and the combating of the corruption of character and of everything liable to bear on society's values, explaining that among the manifestations of corruption is the spreading of falsehood, reminding those present of the muslim's duty towards his community and his homeland, warning the young in particular against narcotics and acts of disobedience, and pointing out that the soundness of society begins with the individual, then the family, then the neighbours. he enumerated a set of factors of reform, such as calling people to god, teaching people what is good, enjoining the truth upon one another, strengthening the spirit of islamic brotherhood and of mutual support, coming to the aid of the wronged, and preventing the wrongdoer from his wrongdoing — citing the saying of the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace: "aid your brother, whether he is a wrongdoer or wronged. a man said: messenger of god, i aid him when he is wronged — but tell me, when he is a wrongdoer, how do i aid him? he said: you restrain him, or you prevent him from wrongdoing; for that is aiding him." he also called for working to change what is wrong by lawful means; affirming that nations are built upon values, and that the voter's vote is a trust upon his neck, so that it is not permissible to sell it or to exploit it for anything other than the truth, because the selling of votes is a participation in corruption and a corrupting of public affairs — calling for the awareness of god almighty's watching to be brought to mind when this trust is discharged. he also spoke on the question of provision and earning, explaining that the haste of some young people to amass money may drive them to take forbidden paths, affirming that provision is already written, and that the believer is required to seek out what is lawful and to keep away from usurious gain (ribā) and from all other forbidden earnings, for what they bring of ruinous effects upon individuals and societies; and that turning towards god almighty and being conscious of him are among the greatest causes of blessing and of ample provision. he affirmed that bearing responsibility is reckoned among the most important factors of the soundness of societies, for every individual is a partner in building his homeland and serving his society, and he ought not to wait for someone else to carry out the reform; rather he must contribute to the public good and take care not to be a cause of the spreading of corruption or of acts of disobedience, or a means of making known what the adversaries of islam want, who seek the ruin of societies — affirming that it is part of complete faith that the muslim be a key to what is good and one who calls to virtue and to reform. the programme continues in the coming days with lectures, classes and scholarly and da'wah meetings with the city's scholars, its imams and its notables, within the framework of strengthening contact and cooperation in the service of da'wah, spreading sharia knowledge, answering the questions of those who frequent and maintain the mosques, establishing the values of balance and moderation, urging the young to hold fast to the book and the sunnah, and contributing to the building of society on the foundations of knowledge, faith and character. the sheikh's programme for this year aims to bring together the cultivation of faith and grounding in scholarship, by raising questions that touch the reality of the muslims, that bind them to the foundations of their religion, and that help them to understand the sharia rulings and to apply them in their daily lives, in a manner that combines clarity of presentation with argument from the book and the sunnah and with drawing on the statements of the scholars and their independent reasoning (ijtihād). the programme takes up a series of subjects that establish religious values, foremost among them the factors of the reform of societies, coming to the aid of the muslims, love for the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, and following his sunnah — alongside setting out the standing of knowledge and the merit of learning it, urging its dissemination and its being brought within reach, the embracing of its students and care for its institutions, holding fast to the way of the righteous predecessors, and establishing the meanings of islamic brotherhood and unity and the casting off of the causes of division and dispute.

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Concludes This Year's Summer Scholarly and Da'wah Programme with Four Scholarly Lectures
a: الشيخ الددو يختتم برنامجه العلمي والدعوي الصيفي لهذا العام بأربع محاضرات علمية،
b: his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan ould al-dedew concluded this year's summer scholarly and da'wah programme with four scholarly lectures, which saw a wide attendance and turnout from the people of the city of nouadhibou, and from which a great throng of scholars, callers to islam and students of knowledge of both sexes benefited. the sheikh began his programme with a lecture entitled "the standing of knowledge and the merit of learning and teaching it", hosted by the al-jawdah centre for the sharia sciences, in which his eminence set out the rank of sharia knowledge, the merit of its people, and the importance of sincerity (ikhlāṣ) in seeking and teaching it, calling on the people of the city to encourage the seeking of knowledge and to support and care for its institutions — for knowledge is the foundation of the ummah's renaissance and its soundness. as for the second lecture, it came under the title "the factors of the soundness of societies and the combating of corruption and of corrupting", in which he took up the causes that lead to the uprightness of societies — foremost among them the establishing of faith, the setting up of justice, and enjoining right and forbidding wrong — warning of the effects of corruption and of corrupting upon individuals and nations, and enumerating examples of the bad customs and characters that it is the community's duty to combat and to stand against, such as acts of disobedience, the taking of narcotics, wrongdoing, consuming the wealth of others, and not discharging rights and trusts. the sheikh opened the second day's programme with a sharia session hosted by the quba congregational mosque, which saw a large attendance from the people of the city, before delivering, after the afternoon prayer on wednesday, his third lecture, entitled "convey from me, even a single verse", at the al-ridwan mosque in the city of nouadhibou — which was among the activities of the 2026 da'wah mobilisation organised by the al-mustaqbal association for da'wah, culture and education — where he spoke about what the testimony of god's oneness requires, the means of calling people to god, and the responsibility of every muslim to convey the religion of god according to his capacity; and he urged the confronting of the devils among humankind and among the jinn by spreading what is good and making people desire to call others to god and to hold fast to the book and the sunnah. the programme's activities were concluded with a lecture entitled "cultural work as da'wah and as worship", organised by the two associations shabibat bina' al-watan and al-fatat for awareness and upbringing, in which his eminence took up the standing of the young and their pivotal role in making society aware, in reforming it and in building nations — affirming that purposeful cultural work is reckoned among the means of calling people to god and of serving religion and society, if the intention in it is kept sincere and the purpose is sound. the programme also took in visits to some of the scholars and callers to islam, as well as his eminence the sheikh's receiving, at his place of residence, dozens of scholarly and da'wah figures, and groups of the city's professionals, its notables and its people, in which scholarly and da'wah meetings took place that took up questions of thought, of da'wah and of upbringing, and the urging of care for students of knowledge; and they were concluded with a supplication for success and right direction, and that god set right both the present state and the end.
